briefDescription: Used to express a contrast between two nouns. Similar to: N에 비해서 (No. 254).
featuredTranslation: Unlike the older brother, the younger brother has an active personality.
longerExplanation: This structure is used to highlight a specific difference in quality, behavior, or state between two subjects. It functions as an adverbial phrase.

sentenceExamples.en: Unlike our expectations, the exam was very easy.

sentenceExamples.kr: 서울과 달리 이 도시는 조용하고 깨끗해요.
sentenceExamples.en: Unlike Seoul, this city is quiet and clean.
Unlike yesterday, the weather is clear today.

name: N에 따라(서)
englishMeaning: According to N / Depending on N
briefDescription: Indicates that the following action or result changes based on the noun.
featuredTranslation: Cultures differ depending on the country.
longerExplanation: Used to show that a situation is variable. The result in the second clause is determined by the standard or criteria set by the noun in the first clause.

sentenceExamples.kr: 사람에 따라 생각이 다를 수 있어요.
sentenceExamples.en: Thoughts can differ depending on the person.
Choose the color according to your preference.

sentenceExamples.kr: 날씨에 따라 계획이 바뀔 수도 있습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Plans may change depending on the weather.

name: N에 불과하다
englishMeaning: Is merely N / Is nothing more than N
briefDescription: Used to downplay or belittle the amount or importance of a noun.
featuredTranslation: This is merely the beginning.
longerExplanation: This is a formal/written expression used to show that something does not exceed a certain (usually low) level or standard. It often carries a nuance of limitation.

sentenceExamples.en: That rumor is nothing more than a lie.
Merely 10% of the participants agreed.
He is merely an acquaintance to me.

name: N만 못하다
englishMeaning: Not as good as N / Inferior to N
briefDescription: Used to say that something is of lower quality or degree than N.
featuredTranslation: The younger brother is not as good as the older brother.
longerExplanation: This is a comparative structure that establishes 'N' as the superior standard. It implies that the subject fails to reach the level of N.

sentenceExamples.en: The taste is not as good as it used to be.
This movie is not as good as the original novel.

sentenceExamples.kr: 건강을 잃으면 돈은 아무것도 아닌 것만 못하다.
sentenceExamples.en: If you lose health, money is worse than having nothing (not as good as nothing).

name: V-(으)ㄹ 게 아니라
englishMeaning: Instead of doing V / Don't just V, but...
briefDescription: Suggests a better alternative to the current or planned action.
featuredExample: 걱정만 할 게 아니라 직접 가서 확인해 보세요.
featuredTranslation: Instead of just worrying, go there yourself and check.
longerExplanation: Used to correct someone's behavior or intended plan by providing a more logical or productive alternative. It usually follows with a command or suggestion.

sentenceExamples.kr: 집에만 있을 게 아니라 산책이라도 나갑시다.
sentenceExamples.en: Instead of just staying home, let's at least go for a walk.

sentenceExamples.kr: 불평할 게 아니라 해결 방법을 찾아야 해요.
sentenceExamples.en: Instead of complaining, we need to find a solution.

sentenceExamples.kr: 말만 할 게 아니라 행동으로 보여 주세요.
sentenceExamples.en: Don't just talk, show it through actions.

name: N(으)로서
briefDescription: Indicates the status, position, or qualification of a person. Similar to: N(으)로써 (Tool/Means).
featuredTranslation: As a teacher, he loves his students.
longerExplanation: '-로서' is used for people and their roles. It explains the 'hat' someone is wearing while they perform an action or hold an opinion. (Note: Do not confuse with '-(으)로써' which is used for tools or methods).

sentenceExamples.en: As a friend, I'll give you one piece of advice.
As a parent, the child's happiness is the most important.
He participated in the competition as a representative of Korea.

name: A-다기보다는, V-ㄴ/는 다기보다는
englishMeaning: Rather than calling it X / It's not so much X as Y
briefDescription: Used to say that one description is more accurate than another.
featuredTranslation: Rather than calling it scary, that movie was sad.
longerExplanation: Used when the speaker wants to refine a description. It acknowledges that the first term might be used, but the second term is a more precise or suitable fit for the situation.

sentenceExamples.en: It's not so much that I hate it as I'm just not interested.
Rather than saying I succeeded, I think I was just lucky.
It wasn't that I was busy so much as I didn't feel like going (it was bothersome).

name: 설마 A/V-겠어요?
englishMeaning: No way... right? / Surely it wouldn't...
briefDescription: Expresses strong disbelief or the hope that something negative won't happen.
featuredTranslation: Surely that rumor wouldn't be true, right?
longerExplanation: The adverb '설마' signals that the speaker finds a situation hard to believe. When paired with the presumptive '-겠어요', it seeks confirmation that the unlikely/negative event is not the reality.

sentenceExamples.kr: 설마 비가 오겠어요? 하늘이 이렇게 맑은데요.
sentenceExamples.en: Surely it won't rain? The sky is so clear.
No way you've eaten it all already, right?
Surely he haven't forgotten me?

name: N(으)로부터
briefDescription: Indicates the starting point or source. Similar to: N에게서 (No. 66).
featuredTranslation: I received a gift from a friend.
longerExplanation: Used for formal situations or when describing the origin of a feeling, a piece of information, or a physical object. It is often used with inanimate sources (like organizations) but can be used for people too.

sentenceExamples.en: I want to be independent from my parents.
We came to receive support from the government.
That news was delivered from the media.

name: A-다 싶다, V-ㄴ/는 다 싶다
englishMeaning: I have a feeling that... / It seems to me that...
briefDescription: Expresses a subjective thought or an impression. Similar to: -ㄴ 것 같다 (No. 1).
featuredTranslation: I felt that this was enough, so I stopped.
longerExplanation: Used when the speaker has an inner thought or intuition. It describes a 'subjective sense' or a conclusion reached in the speaker's mind based on their perception of the situation.

sentenceExamples.en: If you have a feeling it's wrong, fix it immediately.
Feeling that it was too late, I hurried out.
Thinking it would be tasty, I tried buying one.

name: A/V-았었/었었-
briefDescription: Indicates a past state or action that is completely over and no longer exists. Similar to: -았던/었던 (No. 220).
featuredTranslation: I used to be very fat when I was young (but I'm not now).
longerExplanation: The 'double past' creates a distance between the past event and the present. It emphasizes that the state in the past is finished and is often used to contrast the past with a different current reality.

sentenceExamples.en: I lived in Korea until last year (implying I don't now).
I used to be unable to eat spicy food (implying I can now).

sentenceExamples.kr: 그 사람을 한 번 만났었었는데 기억이 안 나요.
sentenceExamples.en: I had met that person once in the past, but I don't remember.

name: V-는 사이(에)
englishMeaning: While / During the interval of V
briefDescription: Indicates that an unexpected event happened while an action was occurring. Similar to: -는 동안 (No. 32).
featuredTranslation: While I was dozing off for a moment, I passed my stop.
longerExplanation: Focuses on a short or specific interval of time during which something else happened (often unexpectedly). It can have different subjects in each clause.

sentenceExamples.kr: 엄마가 전화를 받는 사이에 아기가 울기 시작했어요.
sentenceExamples.en: While mom was answering the phone, the baby started crying.

sentenceExamples.kr: 도둑이 내가 한눈을 파는 사이에 지갑을 훔쳐갔어요.
sentenceExamples.en: The thief stole my wallet while I was looking away.
While I was resting for a bit, the rain stopped.

name: A-다는 N, V-ㄴ/는다는 N
briefDescription: Used to describe a noun using a reported statement. Similar to: -다고 하는 N.
featuredTranslation: I heard the news that there is an exam tomorrow.
longerExplanation: This is a noun-modifying form for indirect quotations. It is used when the following noun (like news, rumor, fact, promise) content is the clause that precedes it.

sentenceExamples.en: The rumor that he succeeded is widespread.
I kept the promise that we would meet again.
The fact that he is not the culprit was revealed.

name: A-(으)ㄴ지 A-(으)ㄴ지, V-는지 V-는지
briefDescription: Used to list options when the speaker is unsure. Similar to: -든지 (No. 116).
featuredTranslation: I'm not sure if he is a student or a teacher.
longerExplanation: Commonly followed by verbs of 'knowing' or 'inquiring' (모르다, 알다, 물어보다). It expresses a choice between two or more possibilities where the exact answer is unknown.

sentenceExamples.kr: 비가 오는지 안 오는지 확인해 보세요.
sentenceExamples.en: Check whether it's raining or not.
I don't know if this is correct or wrong.

sentenceExamples.kr: 어디가 아픈지 왜 아픈지 말해 봐.
sentenceExamples.en: Tell me where it hurts and why it hurts.

name: A-다는 것은 N에서/N(으)로 알 수 있다
englishMeaning: The fact that X can be seen from N
briefDescription: Formal structure used to provide evidence for a statement.
featuredExample: 그가 성실하다는 것은 그의 행동에서 알 수 있어요.
featuredTranslation: The fact that he is sincere can be seen from his actions.
longerExplanation: This is a logical concluding structure often used in essays or speeches. It presents a 'truth' in the first part and points to the 'proof' or 'source' in the second part.

sentenceExamples.kr: 한국 문화가 인기 있다는 것은 통계로 알 수 있습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: The fact that Korean culture is popular can be seen through statistics.

sentenceExamples.kr: 환경이 오염됐다는 것은 공기 상태에서 알 수 있어요.
sentenceExamples.en: The fact that the environment is polluted can be seen from the state of the air.

sentenceExamples.kr: 실력이 늘었다는 것은 시험 점수로 알 수 있습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: The fact that skills improved can be seen from the exam scores.

name: A-다고요? / V-ㄴ/는다고요?
englishMeaning: Are you saying that...? / Did you say...?
briefDescription: Used to confirm or ask again about something the listener just said. Similar to: -다고 하다 (No. 234).
featuredTranslation: Are you saying there's an exam tomorrow? I really didn't know.
longerExplanation: This is an exclamatory or interrogative version of indirect speech. It is used when the speaker is surprised by what they heard and wants to double-check, or when they want to emphasize a point they just made to someone who didn't hear properly.

sentenceExamples.en: Are you saying you ate it all already? That was really fast.
Did you say that person is debuting as a singer?
I told you yesterday. I said I'm not going.

name: V-(으)ㄹ 생각[계획/예정]이다
englishMeaning: I am thinking of/planning to V
briefDescription: Used to express a specific future plan or intention. Similar to: -(으)려고 하다 (No. 13).
featuredTranslation: I am planning to go to Jeju Island this vacation.
longerExplanation: This structure is more concrete than a simple 'wish'. Using '생각' implies a thought, '계획' implies a solid plan, and '예정' implies a fixed schedule. It is frequently used in formal interviews or when discussing official projects.

sentenceExamples.en: I am scheduled (plan) to enter graduate school after graduation.
I'm thinking of quitting my job and starting a business.
I have plans to have a party with friends tomorrow.

name: V-이/히/리/기/우- (사동)
briefDescription: Suffixes added to verbs to show the subject makes someone else perform an action. Similar to: -게 하다 (No. 84).
featuredTranslation: The mother feeds milk to the baby (makes the baby eat).
longerExplanation: These suffixes turn active verbs into causative ones. 먹다 (eat) -> 먹이다 (feed), 자다 (sleep) -> 재우다 (put to sleep), 웃다 (laugh) -> 웃기다 (make laugh). Unlike '-게 하다', these are often single-word lexicalized forms.

sentenceExamples.en: I made my sibling sit on the chair.

sentenceExamples.kr: 가방이 너무 무거워서 제 동생에게 맡겼어요.
sentenceExamples.en: The bag was so heavy I made my sibling carry/handle it.
This news made me laugh.

name: A-다면, V-ㄴ/는다면, N(이)라면
briefDescription: Used to express a hypothetical situation that is unlikely to happen. Similar to: -(으)면 (No. 21).
featuredExample: 내가 부자라면 가난한 사람들을 돕고 싶어요.
featuredTranslation: If I were rich (hypothetically), I would want to help the poor.
longerExplanation: While '-(으)면' is used for general 'if/when', '-다면' is used when the speaker is imagining something that is currently not true or is very unlikely. It often pairs with '-었을 텐데' or '-었을 거예요' in the result clause.

sentenceExamples.en: If I were to be born again, I'd want to be a bird.
If the Earth were to end tomorrow, what would you do?

sentenceExamples.kr: 그 소문이 사실이라면 정말 충격적일 거예요.
sentenceExamples.en: If that rumor were true, it would be truly shocking.

name: 무엇이든(지), 무슨 N(이)든(지)
briefDescription: Indicates that the choice does not matter. Similar to: N(이)나 (No. 69).
featuredExample: 먹고 싶은 것은 무엇이든지 다 시키세요.
featuredTranslation: Order whatever (anything) you want to eat.
longerExplanation: Used to express that any option within a category is acceptable. It implies total inclusiveness or indifference to the selection. It can be used with all question words: 언제든지 (anytime), 어디든지 (anywhere), 누구든지 (anyone).

sentenceExamples.en: No matter what work it is, you must do your best.

sentenceExamples.kr: 어느 것이든지 마음에 드는 것을 고르세요.
sentenceExamples.en: Choose whichever one you like.

sentenceExamples.kr: 누구든지 이 문을 열 수 있습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Anyone can open this door.

name: V-았더니 / 었더니
englishMeaning: Since I did... (I found that / And then)
briefDescription: Used when the speaker's past action leads to a discovery or a result. Similar to: -니까 (No. 20).
featuredExample: 어제 약을 먹었더니 이제 좀 괜찮아요.
featuredTranslation: Since I took medicine yesterday, I feel a bit better now.
longerExplanation: This is specifically for the first person ('I'). It describes an action 'I' did in the past and the immediate result or realization that followed. It often shows a cause-and-effect relationship between the speaker's action and a new state.

sentenceExamples.en: I opened the window, and (then) a cool breeze came in.

sentenceExamples.kr: 열심히 공부했더니 시험 점수가 잘 나왔어요.
sentenceExamples.en: Since I studied hard, I got a good exam score.
I called my friend, but (I found that) he didn't answer.

name: V-고 보니
briefDescription: Used when the speaker realizes something new after an action is fully completed. Similar to: -다 보니까 (No. 217).
featuredTranslation: After finishing the homework, I realized it was 2 AM.
longerExplanation: This structure emphasizes the 'point of completion'. Only after the action was completely over did the speaker look back and notice a fact or feel a certain way. It often carries a nuance of surprise or regret.

sentenceExamples.kr: 가방을 사고 보니 집에 비슷한 것이 있었어요.
sentenceExamples.en: After buying the bag, I realized I had a similar one at home.

sentenceExamples.kr: 음식을 다 먹고 보니 고기가 들어 있었네요.
sentenceExamples.en: After eating all the food, I realized it had meat in it.

sentenceExamples.kr: 이야기를 다 듣고 보니 제 잘못인 것 같아요.
sentenceExamples.en: After hearing the whole story, it seems like it's my fault.

name: A-다니까(요) / V-ㄴ/는다니까(요) / N-(이)라니까(요)
englishMeaning: I told you that... / As I said...
briefDescription: Used to strongly repeat a fact or reason to someone who doesn't seem to believe or understand. Similar to: -다니(까) (No. 191).
featuredExample: 진짜라니까요! 제 말을 좀 믿어 주세요.
featuredTranslation: I'm telling you it's the truth! Please believe me.
longerExplanation: This is a very emphatic spoken ending. It combines indirect speech with the reason particle '-니까'. It is used when the speaker feels frustrated because the listener is ignoring their previous statement or advice.

sentenceExamples.en: As I said, that movie has already finished.

sentenceExamples.kr: 지금 가면 늦는다니까 왜 자꾸 서둘러요?
sentenceExamples.en: I told you we'll be late if we go now, so why are you rushing?
I'm telling you, I am a student. Please give me a discount.

name: 아무리 A/V-아도/어도
briefDescription: Emphasizes that even with an extreme effort or state, the result does not change. Similar to: -아/어도 (No. 8).
featuredTranslation: No matter how much I study, my score doesn't go up.
longerExplanation: Adding the adverb '아무리' (to what extent) before the concessive '-아/어도' creates a very strong emphasis on futility or persistence. It is used to show that the second clause is true regardless of the intensity of the first clause.

sentenceExamples.kr: 아무리 바빠도 밥은 꼭 챙겨 드세요.
sentenceExamples.en: No matter how busy you are, make sure to eat.
No matter how much I think about it, I don't understand.
No matter how hard it is, don't give up.

name: N치고
briefDescription: Used to show that a certain fact applies to all members of a category. Similar to: N마다 (No. 73).
featuredTranslation: There is no human (without exception) who dislikes money.
longerExplanation: Unlike 'N치고는' (which means 'considering the standard'), this version expresses a universal truth. It is almost always followed by a negative ending like '없다' or '않다' to mean 'There is no [N] that doesn't...'.

sentenceExamples.kr: 아이치고 초콜릿을 안 좋아하는 아이가 있을까요?
sentenceExamples.en: Is there any child (without exception) who doesn't like chocolate?

sentenceExamples.kr: 운동선수치고 몸이 약한 사람은 본 적이 없어요.
sentenceExamples.en: I've never seen an athlete who has a weak body.

sentenceExamples.kr: 한국 사람치고 김치를 모르는 사람은 없다.
sentenceExamples.en: There is no Korean person who doesn't know Kimchi.

name: A/V-(으)ㄴ가/는가 (하다/보다)
briefDescription: A formal interrogative form used to express a logical conjecture or self-question. Similar to: -나 보다 (No. 90).
featuredExample: 무슨 좋은 일이 있는가 해서 물어봤어요.
featuredTranslation: I asked because I wondered if something good was happening.
longerExplanation: Found in SNU Book 4. It is a formal way to speculate or present a question to oneself. It is often paired with '하다' or '보다' to show the speaker is thinking through a possibility based on observation.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그의 말이 사실인가 해서 확인해 봤어요.
sentenceExamples.en: I wondered if his words were true, so I checked.
I thought to myself, 'I guess the exam is difficult'.
I looked outside wondering if someone had come.

name: N(이)면 N
englishMeaning: If it's N, then N (The best/The absolute)
briefDescription: Used to emphasize that a specific noun is the perfect representative of its category.
featuredExample: 노래면 노래, 춤이면 춤, 그녀는 완벽한 스타예요.
featuredTranslation: Whether it's singing or dancing, she is a perfect star.
longerExplanation: This structure repeats the noun to show that the subject is an expert or possesses all qualities related to that noun. It’s like saying 'From A to Z regarding N, this person/thing is the best.'

sentenceExamples.kr: 겨울 스포츠면 겨울 스포츠, 그는 못하는 게 없어요.
sentenceExamples.en: When it comes to winter sports, there is nothing he can't do.

sentenceExamples.kr: 음식하면 음식, 분위기하면 분위기, 이 식당이 최고예요.
sentenceExamples.en: The food, the atmosphere—this restaurant is top-tier in every way.

sentenceExamples.kr: 이론이면 이론, 실기면 실기, 부족한 게 없습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Theory or practice, it's perfect; nothing is lacking.

name: A/V-(으)ㄴ가/는가 하면
englishMeaning: While X is true, on the other hand Y...
briefDescription: Used to connect two contrasting or diverse facts about a situation. Similar to: -는 반면에 (No. 112).
featuredExample: 야채를 좋아하는 사람이 있는가 하면 고기를 좋아하는 사람도 있어요.
featuredTranslation: While there are people who like vegetables, there are also people who like meat.
longerExplanation: Found in SNU Book 4, pg 72. It is used to describe diversity or multiple existing realities within a group. It highlights that while one state (A) exists, a different or opposite state (B) also exists simultaneously.

sentenceExamples.kr: 날씨가 맑은가 하면 갑자기 비가 오기도 해요.
sentenceExamples.en: While the weather is clear, it also suddenly rains sometimes.

sentenceExamples.kr: 공부를 잘하는 학생이 있는가 하면 운동을 잘하는 학생도 있다.
sentenceExamples.en: While some students are good at academics, others are good at sports.

sentenceExamples.kr: 가격이 싼가 하면 품질이 좋은 제품도 많습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: While some prices are cheap, there are also many high-quality products.

name: (A-(으)ㄴ/V-는) N에 (A-(으)ㄴ/V-는) N
englishMeaning: N after N / N upon N
briefDescription: Used to describe many different things being stacked or added together. Similar to: N에다가 N (In addition to).
featuredExample: 모르는 단어에 모르는 문법에, 정말 읽기 힘들어요.
featuredTranslation: Unknown words upon unknown grammar; it's really hard to read.
longerExplanation: This pattern is used to emphasize that multiple items or situations are piling up, usually creating a feeling of being overwhelmed. It repeats the descriptive form (Modifier + Noun) to show a cumulative effect.

sentenceExamples.kr: 비싼 가격에 비싼 관리비에, 그 아파트는 포기했어요.
sentenceExamples.en: The expensive price on top of the expensive maintenance fees made me give up on that apartment.

sentenceExamples.kr: 바쁜 업무에 바쁜 집안일에, 눈코 뜰 새 없이 지내고 있어요.
sentenceExamples.en: Between the busy work and the busy housework, I'm incredibly busy.

sentenceExamples.kr: 매운 음식에 매운 소스에, 속이 너무 아파요.
sentenceExamples.en: With spicy food on top of spicy sauce, my stomach hurts so much.

name: N(까지)는 못 돼도 N은/는 A/V-(으)ㄹ 줄 알았다
englishMeaning: Even if it couldn't reach X, I thought it would at least be Y
briefDescription: Used to express a minimum expectation that was not met. Similar to: -줄 알았다 (No. 192).
featuredExample: 1등은 못 돼도 합격은 할 줄 알았어요.
featuredTranslation: Even if I couldn't get first place, I thought I would at least pass.
longerExplanation: This complex structure expresses disappointment. The speaker admits that a high goal (the first N) might have been difficult, but they had a solid expectation for a lower, more realistic goal (the second N) which still wasn't achieved.

sentenceExamples.kr: 부자는 못 돼도 빚은 없을 줄 알았는데.
sentenceExamples.en: I didn't expect to be rich, but I thought at least I wouldn't have debt.

sentenceExamples.kr: 칭찬은 못 돼도 욕은 안 먹을 줄 알았어요.
sentenceExamples.en: I didn't expect praise, but I thought at least I wouldn't be insulted.

sentenceExamples.kr: 프로 선수는 못 돼도 대표팀에는 뽑힐 줄 알았습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Even if I didn't become a pro, I thought I'd at least be picked for the national team.

name: V-는 둥 마는 둥
englishMeaning: To barely do V / To do V half-heartedly
briefDescription: Describes an action done incompletely due to distraction or haste. Similar to: 대충 (Carelessly).
featuredExample: 늦잠을 자서 아침을 먹는 둥 마는 둥 했어요.
featuredTranslation: I overslept, so I barely ate any breakfast.
longerExplanation: Literally 'Doing it or not doing it.' It implies that even if the action happened, it was so quick or distracted that it was almost like it didn't happen at all. Often used with verbs like eating, sleeping, or listening.

sentenceExamples.kr: 어제는 걱정이 많아서 잠을 자는 둥 마는 둥 했어요.
sentenceExamples.en: I was so worried yesterday that I barely slept a wink.

sentenceExamples.kr: 바빠서 보고서를 읽는 둥 마는 둥 하고 제출해 버렸어요.
sentenceExamples.en: I was in a rush, so I barely skimmed the report before submitting it.

sentenceExamples.kr: 선생님 말씀을 듣는 둥 마는 둥 하더니 실수를 했네요.
sentenceExamples.en: He barely listened to the teacher and ended up making a mistake.

name: A/V-다는 소리를 듣다
englishMeaning: To hear (others say) that... / To be told that...
briefDescription: Used to mention a reputation or a common comment heard from others. Similar to: -다고 하다 (No. 234).
featuredExample: 저는 어렸을 때부터 똑똑하다는 소리를 많이 들었어요.
featuredTranslation: I've been told I'm smart since I was a child.
longerExplanation: This pattern reports what people generally say about the subject. It is often used to describe one's character, personality, or a recurring piece of feedback from social circles.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그 사람은 성격이 좋다는 소리를 자주 들어요.
sentenceExamples.en: That person is often told that they have a good personality.

sentenceExamples.kr: 너 요즘 예뻐졌다는 소리 안 들어?
sentenceExamples.en: Haven't people been telling you that you've gotten prettier lately?

sentenceExamples.kr: 게으르다는 소리를 안 들으려면 부지런히 일해야 해.
sentenceExamples.en: If you don't want to be told you're lazy, you must work diligently.

name: A/V-다는 인상을 주다
briefDescription: Used to describe the first impression or feeling one gives off. Similar to: -아/어 보이다 (No. 150).
featuredTranslation: He gave the impression of being sincere at first meeting.
longerExplanation: Focuses on the perception or 'vibe' an observer gets. It is a formal way to analyze how someone's clothes, behavior, or speech make them appear to the world.

sentenceExamples.en: Because of the flashy clothes, they gave off the impression of being rich.

sentenceExamples.kr: 자신감이 부족하다는 인상을 주지 않도록 조심하세요.
sentenceExamples.en: Be careful not to give the impression that you lack confidence.

sentenceExamples.kr: 이 식당은 아주 위생적이라는 인상을 줍니다.
sentenceExamples.en: This restaurant gives the impression of being very hygienic.

name: V-는 한이 있어도
englishMeaning: Even if it means... / Even if the worst happens
briefDescription: Expresses strong determination regardless of extreme consequences. Similar to: -더라도 (No. 164).
featuredExample: 굶는 한이 있어도 거짓말은 안 해요.
featuredTranslation: Even if it means starving, I won't tell a lie.
longerExplanation: The strongest form of 'even if.' It sets a hypothetical, extreme, and usually negative scenario in the first clause to show that the second clause (the speaker's resolve) is absolute.

sentenceExamples.kr: 욕을 먹는 한이 있어도 제 소신을 굽히지 않겠습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Even if I get criticized, I will not bend my convictions.

sentenceExamples.kr: 밤을 새우는 한이 있어도 이 일은 꼭 끝내야 해요.
sentenceExamples.en: Even if it means staying up all night, I must finish this.

sentenceExamples.kr: 돈을 다 잃는 한이 있어도 다시 도전할 거예요.
sentenceExamples.en: Even if I lose all my money, I will try again.

name: V-는 등 (N에) 재능을 발휘하다
englishMeaning: To exhibit talent in doing V
briefDescription: Used to describe specific activities where someone shows their skill. Similar to: N에 소질이 있다.
featuredExample: 그는 어릴 때부터 요리하는 등 주방에서 재능을 발휘했어요.
featuredTranslation: He has exhibited talent in the kitchen, such as cooking, since he was young.
longerExplanation: Commonly used in biographies or profiles. It lists examples of actions (V-는 등) to prove that someone is gifted in a certain field (N에 재능을 발휘하다).

sentenceExamples.kr: 그녀는 그림을 그리는 등 예술 분야에서 재능을 발휘하고 있습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: She is exhibiting talent in the art field, such as painting.

sentenceExamples.kr: 외국어를 빨리 배우는 등 언어 학습에 재능을 발휘하더군요.
sentenceExamples.en: I noticed they exhibit talent in language learning, such as learning foreign languages quickly.

sentenceExamples.kr: 어려운 문제를 푸는 등 수학에서 뛰어난 재능을 발휘했어요.
sentenceExamples.en: He exhibited outstanding talent in math, such as solving difficult problems.

name: N을/를 시작으로 N을/를 거쳐 N을/를 맡다
englishMeaning: Starting with N, going through N, to taking charge of N
briefDescription: Used to describe a career path or the progression of roles over time.
featuredExample: 그는 사원을 시작으로 부장을 거쳐 현재 사장을 맡고 있다.
featuredTranslation: Starting as an employee, going through manager, he is currently in charge as the CEO.
longerExplanation: A formal way to describe a chronological career trajectory or a sequence of positions held by a person.

sentenceExamples.kr: 기자를 시작으로 앵커를 거쳐 국회의원을 맡게 되었습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Starting as a reporter, moving through news anchor, he came to hold the position of a National Assembly member.

sentenceExamples.kr: 조연을 시작으로 주연을 거쳐 감독까지 맡게 되었어요.
sentenceExamples.en: Starting with supporting roles, through leading roles, he even came to take charge as a director.

sentenceExamples.kr: 인턴을 시작으로 팀장을 거쳐 본부장을 맡고 있습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Starting as an intern, through team leader, he is currently in charge as head of headquarters.

name: V-(으)ㄴ 바 있다
englishMeaning: There is a history of V / As has been V-ed
briefDescription: A formal way to mention a past experience or a previously stated fact. Similar to: -(으)ㄴ 적이 있다 (No. 4).
featuredExample: 앞서 언급한 바와 같이 이 문제는 심각합니다.
featuredTranslation: As mentioned previously, this problem is serious.
longerExplanation: Used primarily in formal writing, speeches, or news reports. It indicates that something happened or was established in the past. When used with '바와 같이', it means 'As already [V-ed]'.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그 회사는 예전에도 세금을 체납한 바 있습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: That company has a history of being delinquent on taxes before.

sentenceExamples.kr: 우리는 이미 이 사건에 대해 조사한 바가 있어요.
sentenceExamples.en: We have already investigated this incident before.
According to the statement the President has released...

name: 너나없이 (모두)
englishMeaning: Everyone without exception / Without distinction of you or me
briefDescription: Used when every person in a group does the same thing. Similar to: 누구나 (No. 238).
featuredExample: 축제 날에는 너나없이 모두 광장으로 모였어요.
featuredTranslation: On the festival day, everyone without exception gathered in the plaza.
longerExplanation: This expression emphasizes complete group participation. It suggests that there was no boundary or difference between people; everyone joined in the action together.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그 소식을 듣고 사람들은 너나없이 기뻐했습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Upon hearing that news, people were happy without exception.

sentenceExamples.kr: 위기가 닥치자 시민들은 너나없이 서로를 도왔어요.
sentenceExamples.en: When the crisis hit, the citizens helped each other without distinction.

sentenceExamples.kr: 유행이 시작되자 너나없이 그 옷을 입기 시작했어요.
sentenceExamples.en: Once the trend started, everyone started wearing those clothes without exception.

name: N(이)나마
englishMeaning: At least / Although it is just...
briefDescription: Expresses that while something isn't perfect, it is better than nothing. Similar to: N(이)라도 (No. 244).
featuredTranslation: Please accept this, even though it's just a small token of my sincerity.
longerExplanation: Used when the speaker acknowledges that the noun is insufficient or disappointing, but offers or accepts it as a compromise. It often carries a nuance of humility.

sentenceExamples.en: I want to apologize for my mistake, even if it's late (at least now).

sentenceExamples.kr: 잠시나마 즐거운 시간을 보낼 수 있어서 좋았어요.
sentenceExamples.en: I was glad to spend a pleasant time, even if it was just for a short while.
Although my skills are lacking, I will do my best.

name: 생각다 못해
englishMeaning: Being unable to think of another way / As a last resort
briefDescription: Used when someone takes an action because they couldn't find any other solution. Similar to: 참다 못해 (No. 176).
featuredExample: 방법이 없어서 생각다 못해 경찰에 신고했어요.
featuredTranslation: Since there was no way, as a last resort, I reported it to the police.
longerExplanation: This phrase describes a state of psychological exhaustion or desperation. The subject has thought and thought, and eventually, out of that 'inability to think further,' they take a decisive (sometimes extreme) step.

sentenceExamples.kr: 혼자 해결하기 힘들어서 생각다 못해 친구에게 전화를 했지.
sentenceExamples.en: It was hard to solve alone, so as a last resort, I called a friend.

sentenceExamples.kr: 돈이 부족해서 생각다 못해 차를 팔기로 했어요.
sentenceExamples.en: I was short on money, so I finally decided to sell the car as a last resort.

sentenceExamples.kr: 고민 끝에 생각다 못해 유학을 포기하기로 했습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: After much agonizing, I eventually decided to give up on studying abroad as a last resort.

name: N(의) 대표적인 예로 N을/를 들다
englishMeaning: To cite N as a representative example of N
briefDescription: Used in presentations or essays to provide a specific, well-known example. Similar to: N-만 해도 (No. 161).
featuredExample: 한국의 정보 통신 기술의 대표적인 예로 반도체를 들 수 있습니다.
featuredTranslation: One can cite semiconductors as a representative example of Korea's IT technology.
longerExplanation: This is a formal academic phrase used to support a general statement with a specific, powerful example. It is essential for TOPIK II Task 54 essays and professional presentations.

sentenceExamples.kr: 성공적인 마케팅의 대표적인 예로 이 브랜드의 광고를 들었습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: I cited this brand's advertisement as a representative example of successful marketing.

sentenceExamples.kr: 환경 오염의 원인 중 대표적인 예로 비닐 사용을 들 수 있어요.
sentenceExamples.en: One can cite the use of plastic as a representative example among the causes of environmental pollution.

sentenceExamples.kr: 한국 문화를 알린 대표적인 예로 케이팝을 들고 싶네요.
sentenceExamples.en: I'd like to cite K-Pop as a representative example that made Korean culture known.

name: 아래와 같이
briefDescription: Used to introduce a list, table, or detailed explanation that follows. Similar to: 다음과 같이.
featuredExample: 회의 결과는 아래와 같이 요약할 수 있습니다.
featuredTranslation: The meeting results can be summarized as follows (shown below).
longerExplanation: A standard phrase used in formal reports, emails, and announcements. It directs the reader's attention to the content presented immediately below the current sentence.

sentenceExamples.kr: 이번 달 행사 일정을 아래와 같이 공지합니다.
sentenceExamples.en: We announce this month's event schedule as follows.

sentenceExamples.kr: 준비물은 아래와 같이 총 세 가지입니다.
sentenceExamples.en: There are three items to prepare in total, as shown below.

sentenceExamples.kr: 아래와 같이 계약 조건을 변경하고자 합니다.
sentenceExamples.en: We intend to change the contract terms as follows.

name: V-(으)오니
briefDescription: A highly formal and humble connective used in official notices or letters. Similar to: -(으)니까 (No. 20).
featuredExample: 공사가 진행 중이오니 우회하여 주시기 바랍니다.
featuredTranslation: As construction is underway, please take a detour.
longerExplanation: This is a very polite and formal version of the 'reason' connector. It is rarely used in speech, but you will see it constantly on signs, public announcements, and formal business letters.

sentenceExamples.en: As there is no class tomorrow, we hope there is no confusion.
As the weather is cold, please take care of your health.

sentenceExamples.kr: 문의 사항이 있으시면 연락 주시오니 친절히 답해 드리겠습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: If you have any inquiries, please contact us and we will answer kindly.

name: N에 한하여
englishMeaning: Limited to N / Only for N
briefDescription: Used to specify a limit or an exclusive condition. Similar to: N-만 (Only).
featuredExample: 이번 세일은 학생증 소지자에 한하여 적용됩니다.
featuredTranslation: This sale is applied only to student ID holders.
longerExplanation: A formal restrictive particle. It is commonly used in legal documents, event guidelines, and promotions to define a specific group or condition that is eligible for something.

sentenceExamples.kr: 참가 자격은 서울 거주자에 한하여 주어집니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Eligibility to participate is given only to Seoul residents.
The parking lot is open for free only on weekends.
Purchase is limited to one per person.

name: N이/가 중요한 역할을 하다
briefDescription: Used to describe the significance of a noun in a certain process or result.
featuredExample: 비타민은 우리 몸에서 중요한 역할을 합니다.
featuredTranslation: Vitamins play an important role in our bodies.
longerExplanation: This phrase identifies a key factor in a system. It is a staple expression in scientific or social essays to emphasize why a particular element is necessary.

sentenceExamples.kr: 교육은 국가 발전에 중요한 역할을 한다고 봅니다.
sentenceExamples.en: I view education as playing an important role in national development.

sentenceExamples.kr: 부모의 태도는 아이의 성격 형성에 중요한 역할을 해요.
sentenceExamples.en: Parents' attitudes play an important role in forming a child's personality.

sentenceExamples.kr: 인터넷은 정보 공유에 있어서 중요한 역할을 수행하고 있습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: The internet is performing an important role in information sharing.

name: N에서 N의 비중이 높다
englishMeaning: N has a high proportion/weight in N
briefDescription: Used in statistics or social analysis to show the importance of a specific part of a whole.
featuredExample: 한국 수출에서 반도체의 비중이 매우 높습니다.
featuredTranslation: Semiconductors have a very high proportion in Korea's exports.
longerExplanation: This describes how much influence or space a specific category occupies within a larger group. '비중' literally means 'relative weight.'

sentenceExamples.kr: 현대 사회에서는 서비스 산업의 비중이 높아지고 있어요.
sentenceExamples.en: In modern society, the weight of the service industry is increasing.

sentenceExamples.kr: 가계 지출에서 식비가 차지하는 비중이 높은 편입니다.
sentenceExamples.en: The proportion of food expenses in household spending is on the higher side.

sentenceExamples.kr: 우리 회사에서 연구 개발의 비중은 절대적입니다.
sentenceExamples.en: In our company, the proportion of research and development is absolute.

name: A/V-(으)면 그만이다
englishMeaning: That's all one needs / It's enough as long as...
briefDescription: Used when the speaker believes one condition is sufficient, regardless of other factors.
featuredExample: 맛만 있으면 그만이지 가격이 뭐가 중요해요?
featuredTranslation: As long as it tastes good, that's all that matters; why is the price important?
longerExplanation: This pattern expresses a simplified or sometimes cynical view. It suggests that if one primary goal is met, nothing else matters. Depending on the context, it can sound pragmatic or irresponsible.

sentenceExamples.en: The thought that it's enough as long as I'm happy is dangerous.

sentenceExamples.kr: 돈만 많이 벌면 그만이라고 생각하는 사람들이 늘고 있어요.
sentenceExamples.en: The number of people who think earning lots of money is all that matters is increasing.

sentenceExamples.kr: 시험만 잘 보면 그만이지 공부 과정은 중요하지 않아요.
sentenceExamples.en: As long as you do well on the exam, that's enough; the study process isn't important.

name: 이래 가지고(서)(야)
englishMeaning: Given this situation / If things stay like this...
briefDescription: Used to criticize a current state and predict that a desired goal will be impossible. Similar to: -아/어서는 (No. 133 similar).
featuredExample: 이래 가지고서야 언제 일을 다 끝내겠어요?
featuredTranslation: Given this situation, when will we ever finish all the work?
longerExplanation: This is a negative conditional. It takes the current unsatisfactory situation (이래 가지고) and asserts that if it continues, the expected positive result (second clause) will never happen.

sentenceExamples.kr: 공부를 이래 가지고야 시험에 합격할 리가 없지.
sentenceExamples.en: If you study like this (so poorly), there's no way you'll pass the exam.

sentenceExamples.kr: 날씨가 이래 가지고서야 소풍을 갈 수 있겠어?
sentenceExamples.en: With the weather like this, do you think we can go on a picnic?

sentenceExamples.kr: 준비가 이래 가지고야 제대로 발표를 하겠니?
sentenceExamples.en: With preparation like this, will you be able to give a proper presentation?

name: V-(으)ㅁ으로써
englishMeaning: By doing V / As a means of doing V
briefDescription: Indicates the method, tool, or means used to achieve a result. Similar to: N-(으)로써.
featuredExample: 꾸준히 운동함으로써 건강을 지킬 수 있습니다.
featuredTranslation: You can protect your health by exercising steadily.
longerExplanation: A formal and literary connector. It turns a verb into a noun (-ㅁ) and adds the 'means' particle (-써). It is a high-level way to describe a functional methodology in essays.

sentenceExamples.en: They increased their market share by developing new technology.
We decided to resolve the misunderstanding by talking to each other.

sentenceExamples.kr: 쓰레기를 줄임으로써 환경 보호에 기여하고 싶습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: I want to contribute to environmental protection by reducing waste.

name: A-(으)ㄴ/V-는 면이 있다
englishMeaning: There is an aspect of... / Has a side that is...
briefDescription: Used to point out a specific characteristic or a 'side' of someone's personality. Similar to: -는 점이 있다.
featuredExample: 그 사람은 차가워 보이지만 따뜻한 면이 있어요.
featuredTranslation: That person looks cold, but they have a warm side.
longerExplanation: Used when describing someone or something that isn't simple. It allows the speaker to acknowledge one trait while introducing a different, perhaps unexpected, 'aspect' or 'side' (면).

sentenceExamples.kr: 이 계획은 완벽해 보이지만 위험한 면이 있습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: This plan looks perfect, but it has a dangerous side.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그 배우는 연기할 때 아주 진지한 면이 있더라고요.
sentenceExamples.en: I noticed that actor has a very serious side when acting.

sentenceExamples.kr: 도심 생활은 편리한 면도 있지만 스트레스가 많은 면도 있어요.
sentenceExamples.en: City life has a convenient side, but it also has a stressful side.

name: A-기 그지없다
briefDescription: Used to emphasize an extreme, limit-breaking state. Similar to: -기 짝이 없다 (No. 301).
featuredTranslation: His words are truly incomparably (endlessly) rude.
longerExplanation: Literally 'without an end (그지).' It is used to express that an adjective is at its absolute maximum level. It often carries a nuance of strong emotion, whether positive (beautiful) or negative (shameful).

sentenceExamples.kr: 이런 큰 상을 받게 되어 영광스럽기 그지없습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: It is an endless honor to receive such a great award.

sentenceExamples.kr: 홀로 계신 어머니를 생각하면 안타깝기 그지없어요.
sentenceExamples.en: Thinking of my mother alone, it is heart-breaking beyond words.

sentenceExamples.kr: 경치가 아름답기 그지없어서 눈을 뗄 수 없었지요.
sentenceExamples.en: The scenery was so incomparably beautiful I couldn't take my eyes off it.

name: A/V-(으)ㅁ에 틀림없다
englishMeaning: There is no doubt that... / Must be...
briefDescription: Expresses strong certainty or conviction about a fact. Similar to: -게 뻔하다 (No. 255).
featuredExample: 열심히 노력하는 걸 보니 성공함에 틀림없어요.
featuredTranslation: Seeing how hard they work, there is no doubt they will succeed.
longerExplanation: This is a logical conclusion. Based on the evidence the speaker has, they are 100% sure the statement is true. It is more formal and authoritative than '-것 같다.'

sentenceExamples.en: Evidence has come out that he is undoubtedly the culprit.
There is no doubt that the rumor yesterday was a lie.

sentenceExamples.kr: 이 요리는 전문가가 만들었음에 틀림없을 정도로 맛있네요.
sentenceExamples.en: This dish is so delicious it must have been made by an expert.

name: 뭐니 뭐니 해도
englishMeaning: Whatever anyone says / All in all / When all is said and done
briefDescription: An idiomatic phrase used to emphasize that a specific thing is the most important or best. Similar to: 무엇보다도.
featuredExample: 뭐니 뭐니 해도 건강이 제일 중요합니다.
featuredTranslation: Whatever anyone says, health is the most important thing.
longerExplanation: Literally translated as 'No matter what [anyone] says or does,' this phrase is used to introduce the speaker's firm opinion on what the top priority or best option in a category is.

sentenceExamples.kr: 한국 음식은 뭐니 뭐니 해도 김치가 최고지요.
sentenceExamples.en: When all is said and done, Kimchi is the best Korean food.

sentenceExamples.kr: 여행은 뭐니 뭐니 해도 마음 맞는 친구와 가는 게 좋아요.
sentenceExamples.en: Whatever anyone says, it's best to go on a trip with a like-minded friend.

sentenceExamples.kr: 뭐니 뭐니 해도 집이 제일 편안한 법이에요.
sentenceExamples.en: All in all, it's natural that home is the most comfortable place.

name: N을/를 계기로
englishMeaning: With N as a turning point / Using N as an opportunity
briefDescription: Indicates that a certain event (N) triggered a major change or a new action. Similar to: N을/를 통해서 (No. 261 similar).
featuredExample: 이번 사고를 계기로 안전 수칙을 강화했습니다.
featuredTranslation: With this accident as a turning point, we strengthened safety regulations.
longerExplanation: Used when an event acts as a catalyst. It explains that because of N, a new situation developed or a significant decision was made. It is very common in news and historical context.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그 영화를 계기로 한국 문화에 관심을 갖게 되었어요.
sentenceExamples.en: With that movie as an opportunity, I came to have an interest in Korean culture.

sentenceExamples.kr: 우리는 대학교 때 봉사 활동을 계기로 처음 만났습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: We first met using a volunteer activity in university as the occasion.

sentenceExamples.kr: 실패를 계기로 삼아 더 열심히 노력하기로 했어요.
sentenceExamples.en: I decided to use the failure as a turning point and work harder.

name: A/V-지(요), 뭐
englishMeaning: Let's just... / I guess I'll... (Casual acceptance)
briefDescription: Used when the speaker makes a decision or gives a suggestion in a cool, casual, or slightly indifferent manner.
featuredExample: 약속이 취소됐으면 그냥 집에서 쉬지, 뭐.
featuredTranslation: If the appointment is canceled, I guess I'll just rest at home.
longerExplanation: This ending shows that the speaker is not overly stressed about a situation and is choosing an easy alternative. It often carries a nuance of 'it's not a big deal, I'll just do this instead.'

sentenceExamples.kr: 배가 안 고프면 나중에 먹지, 뭐.
sentenceExamples.en: If you're not hungry, I guess we'll just eat later.

sentenceExamples.kr: 버스가 안 오면 택시 타고 가지, 뭐.
sentenceExamples.en: If the bus doesn't come, I'll just take a taxi.
If I don't know, I guess I'll just ask the teacher.

name: A/V-다는 거야
englishMeaning: The thing is that... / They're saying that...
briefDescription: Used to summarize or emphasize the core point of what someone said. Similar to: -다는 뜻이다.
featuredTranslation: The point is that we eventually won.
longerExplanation: A conversational contraction of '-다는 것이야'. It is used to clarify the bottom line of a story or to re-explain a complex situation in a single, powerful sentence.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그러니까 그 사람이 범인이 아니라는 거야.
sentenceExamples.en: So, what they're saying is that person is not the culprit.

sentenceExamples.kr: 내 말은 우리가 더 노력해야 한다는 거야.
sentenceExamples.en: My point is that we need to work harder.
Are you saying that the rumor was all a lie?

name: A/V-겠거니 (하다)
briefDescription: Used when the speaker makes a subjective assumption that a certain state or action is obvious.
featuredTranslation: I was waiting, assuming that of course they would come.
longerExplanation: This describes a mental state where the speaker expected something to happen as a matter of course. It is often followed by a result that contrasts with that assumption (e.g., 'I assumed they'd come, but they didn't').

sentenceExamples.kr: 선생님이 도와주겠거니 믿고 공부를 안 했어요.
sentenceExamples.en: Assuming the teacher would help, I didn't study.

sentenceExamples.kr: 비가 곧 그치겠거니 생각해서 우산을 안 챙겼지.
sentenceExamples.en: Thinking the rain would stop soon, I didn't bring an umbrella.

sentenceExamples.kr: 다들 알고 있겠거니 해서 말을 안 했어요.
sentenceExamples.en: I didn't say anything, assuming that everyone already knew.

name: 따지고 보면
englishMeaning: If you look into it closely / Actually / When you think about it
briefDescription: Used to introduce a fact that becomes clear after logical thinking or detailed analysis.
featuredExample: 따지고 보면 그 사람 말도 일리가 있어요.
featuredTranslation: If you think about it, what he says also makes sense.
longerExplanation: This phrase is used to challenge a superficial view. It signals that while the surface situation looks one way, the 'actual' reality or deeper logic is different.

sentenceExamples.kr: 따지고 보면 이게 다 우리를 위한 일이에요.
sentenceExamples.en: Actually, when you look into it, this is all for our benefit.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그 문제는 따지고 보면 아주 간단한 문제였어요.
sentenceExamples.en: If you look closely, that problem was actually a very simple one.

sentenceExamples.kr: 따지고 보면 환경 오염의 책임은 우리 모두에게 있죠.
sentenceExamples.en: When you think about it, the responsibility for environmental pollution lies with all of us.

name: 다시 말해서
englishMeaning: In other words / That is to say
briefDescription: Used to provide a simpler or more direct explanation of a previous statement. Similar to: 즉 (No. 62 similar).
featuredExample: 그는 퇴사했어요. 다시 말해서 이제 우리 직원이 아니에요.
featuredTranslation: He resigned. In other words, he is no longer our employee.
longerExplanation: A logical transition used to rephrase or summarize a complex idea to ensure the listener understands perfectly. It is essential for academic discussions and formal writing.

sentenceExamples.kr: 이건 무료예요. 다시 말해서 돈을 낼 필요가 없다는 뜻이죠.
sentenceExamples.en: This is free. That is to say, you don't need to pay money.

sentenceExamples.kr: 우리는 실패했습니다. 다시 말해서 새로운 계획이 필요해요.
sentenceExamples.en: We failed. In other words, we need a new plan.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그는 천재예요. 다시 말해서 노력 없이도 잘한다는 거죠.
sentenceExamples.en: He is a genius. That is to say, he does well without even trying.

name: V-(으)려는지
englishMeaning: I wonder if [one] intends to... / Seeming to be about to...
briefDescription: Used to express a guess about someone's intentions or a future natural event.
featuredTranslation: I don't know the reason why the child seems to be about to cry.
longerExplanation: This pattern shows the speaker's uncertainty about a future action or intention. It is often used when observing an outward sign (like clouds before rain) and guessing the 'intent' of the situation.

sentenceExamples.kr: 하늘을 보니 비가 오려는지 구름이 몰려오네요.
sentenceExamples.en: Looking at the sky, clouds are gathering as if it's about to rain.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그 사람이 무엇을 도와주려는지 계속 쳐다봐요.
sentenceExamples.en: I wonder if he intends to help with something, as he keeps staring.

sentenceExamples.kr: 내일은 날씨가 좋으려는지 달이 참 밝네요.
sentenceExamples.en: The moon is so bright; I wonder if the weather will be good tomorrow.

name: A/V-거나 하다
englishMeaning: To do something like... / Or do such things
briefDescription: Used to list one or two representative actions/states as examples. Similar to: -거나 (No. 15).
featuredTranslation: On weekends, I usually do things like sleeping.
longerExplanation: Unlike a simple '-거나', adding '하다' at the end makes the action sound more like a general example of a habit or a loose suggestion. It implies 'this is one of the things I do among others.'

sentenceExamples.en: When I'm bored, I do things like reading books.
If you're sick, you should do things like taking medicine or going to the hospital.

sentenceExamples.kr: 스트레스를 받으면 매운 걸 먹거나 해요.
sentenceExamples.en: When I'm stressed, I do things like eating spicy food.

name: N 바람이 불다
englishMeaning: A craze for N is blowing / N trend is spreading
briefDescription: A metaphorical expression describing a sudden social trend or obsession.
featuredExample: 요즘 젊은이들 사이에서 운동 바람이 불고 있어요.
featuredTranslation: An exercise craze is blowing among young people these days.
longerExplanation: Uses the image of 'wind' (바람) to describe a fast-moving social phenomenon. It indicates that a specific activity, product, or mindset has suddenly become very popular.

sentenceExamples.kr: 해외 주식 투자 바람이 불어서 많은 사람들이 계좌를 만들었죠.
sentenceExamples.en: Since the foreign stock investment craze blew, many people created accounts.
A trend for retro fashion has begun to blow.

sentenceExamples.kr: 건강식 바람이 부는 마당에 채식주의자가 늘고 있습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Under the circumstances where a healthy food trend is blowing, vegetarians are increasing.

name: N이자 N
englishMeaning: N and also N / Both N and N
briefDescription: Used to show that a person or thing has two roles or identities simultaneously.
featuredTranslation: He is my teacher and also my friend.
longerExplanation: This particle connects two nouns that describe the same subject. It is commonly used for job titles, relationships, or dual-purpose objects (e.g., 'a bedroom and also a study room').

sentenceExamples.en: This place is a tourist attraction and also a historical site.
She is active as both a singer and an actress.

sentenceExamples.kr: 실패는 성공의 어머니이자 가장 좋은 교훈이죠.
sentenceExamples.en: Failure is the mother of success and also the best lesson.

name: 한편으로(는)
englishMeaning: On one hand / On the other hand
briefDescription: Used to introduce a different or contrasting perspective on the same topic.
featuredExample: 기술의 발전이 기쁘기도 하지만 한편으로는 두렵기도 해요.
featuredTranslation: Technological progress is joyful, but on the other hand, it's also scary.
longerExplanation: This transition word is used to explore the complexity of a situation. After stating one side (A), the speaker uses '한편으로는' to introduce a second, often conflicting, viewpoint (B).

sentenceExamples.kr: 취직해서 좋으면서도 한편으로는 책임감이 무겁게 느껴집니다.
sentenceExamples.en: While I'm glad to be hired, on the other hand, the sense of responsibility feels heavy.

sentenceExamples.kr: 도심 생활은 편리하지만 한편으로는 공해가 심각하죠.
sentenceExamples.en: City life is convenient, but on the other hand, pollution is serious.

sentenceExamples.kr: 성공이 부럽기도 하지만 한편으로는 그 노력이 대단해 보여요.
sentenceExamples.en: I'm envious of the success, but on the other hand, that effort looks amazing.

name: N(이)니 N(이)니 하다
englishMeaning: Saying X and Y / Complaining about X and Y
briefDescription: Used to describe someone listing multiple reasons, excuses, or complaints. Similar to: -니 -니 하다 (No. 322).
featuredExample: 바쁘니 시간이 없니 하면서 핑계만 대요.
featuredTranslation: They just keep making excuses, saying they are busy or have no time.
longerExplanation: This pattern is used to quote various statements made by someone, often with a negative or critical nuance. It suggests that the speaker finds the list of reasons or complaints to be tiresome or insincere.

sentenceExamples.kr: 돈이 없니 비싸니 해도 결국 살 거잖아요.
sentenceExamples.en: Even though you say you have no money or it's expensive, you're going to buy it anyway.

sentenceExamples.kr: 어렵니 못하겠니 하지 말고 일단 해 보세요.
sentenceExamples.en: Stop saying it's hard or you can't do it, and just try it first.

sentenceExamples.kr: 음식이 짜니 맵니 투덜대면서도 다 먹었네요.
sentenceExamples.en: They grumbled about the food being salty or spicy, yet they ate it all.

name: N 여부
englishMeaning: Whether or not N / The status of N
briefDescription: Used to express the binary possibility of a noun (Success/Failure, Participation/Absence).
featuredTranslation: Check the website tomorrow for whether or not you passed.
longerExplanation: A formal noun-based structure used in official documents and news. It combines a hanja-based noun with '여부' (Yes/No) to discuss a result that is not yet determined.

sentenceExamples.kr: 참석 여부를 오늘까지 알려 주시기 바랍니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Please let us know whether or not you will attend by today.

sentenceExamples.kr: 사실 여부가 확인될 때까지 기다려 봅시다.
sentenceExamples.en: Let's wait until the truth of the matter (whether it is a fact or not) is confirmed.

sentenceExamples.kr: 성공 여부에 관계없이 최선을 다했다는 것이 중요해요.
sentenceExamples.en: Regardless of whether it's a success or not, the fact that you did your best is important.

name: N을/를 바탕으로
englishMeaning: Based on N / Founded on N
briefDescription: Indicates that N is the foundation or primary source for a result. Similar to: N에 기초하여.
featuredTranslation: I wrote a novel based on my actual experiences.
longerExplanation: This describes the underlying source material or evidence used to create something new. It is a very common phrase in academic writing, reporting, and discussing creative works.

sentenceExamples.kr: 연구 결과를 바탕으로 대책을 마련해야 합니다.
sentenceExamples.en: We must prepare measures based on the research results.
This movie was produced based on a true story.
Human relationships based on trust are important.

name: 이상에서 본 바와 같이
englishMeaning: As seen from the above / As mentioned earlier
briefDescription: A formal transition used to summarize points previously discussed. Similar to: 앞서 말한 것과 같이.
featuredExample: 이상에서 본 바와 같이 경제 위기는 심각한 수준입니다.
featuredTranslation: As seen from the points above, the economic crisis is at a serious level.
longerExplanation: A standard academic 'summary' phrase used at the end of a presentation or an essay section. It signals to the reader/listener that you are now drawing a conclusion from the facts presented.

sentenceExamples.kr: 이상에서 본 바와 같이 우리는 새로운 대안을 찾아야 합니다.
sentenceExamples.en: As discussed above, we must find a new alternative.

sentenceExamples.kr: 이상에서 본 바와 같이 환경 보호는 더 이상 미룰 수 없는 과제입니다.
sentenceExamples.en: As seen above, environmental protection is a task that can no longer be delayed.

sentenceExamples.kr: 이상에서 본 바와 같이 두 제도는 명확한 차이점이 있습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: As seen above, the two systems have clear differences.

name: V-(으)ㄴ 후에야 (비로소)
englishMeaning: Only after V / Not until V
briefDescription: Emphasizes that a result finally happened only after a specific action. Similar to: -아/어서야 (No. 133).
featuredExample: 사고가 난 후에야 비로소 안전의 소중함을 깨달았어요.
featuredTranslation: Only after the accident happened did I finally realize the importance of safety.
longerExplanation: Adding '-야' and '비로소' to the standard 'after' pattern (-ㄴ 후에) creates strong emphasis. It suggests a sense of regret or a late realization that Action A was a strict requirement for Action B.

sentenceExamples.kr: 부모가 된 후에야 부모님의 마음을 이해하게 되었습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Not until I became a parent did I finally come to understand my parents' hearts.

sentenceExamples.kr: 건강을 잃은 후에야 비로소 규칙적인 운동을 시작했어요.
sentenceExamples.en: Only after losing my health did I finally start exercising regularly.
Only after the exam ended did the tension finally release.

name: A/V-(으)ㄴ들
briefDescription: Used to say that even if a certain condition is met, the expected result is impossible. Similar to: -아/어도 (No. 8).
featuredTranslation: No matter how much you regret it, it's already in the past.
longerExplanation: A literary and rhetorical concessive ending. It is often used to emphasize futility. It basically asks: 'Even if [X] is true, what use is it?' or 'How could [X] change the outcome?'

sentenceExamples.kr: 돈이 많은들 건강을 잃으면 무슨 소용이 있겠어요?
sentenceExamples.en: Even if you have a lot of money, what use is it if you lose your health?
No matter how pretty one is, it's useless if the personality is bad.

sentenceExamples.kr: 과거를 그리워한들 다시 돌아갈 수는 없다.
sentenceExamples.en: Even if you long for the past, you cannot go back.

name: A/V-되
briefDescription: Used to acknowledge the first clause but add a condition or a contrasting point. Similar to: -지만 (No. 162).
featuredTranslation: You may drink, but do not drink excessively.
longerExplanation: A formal and literary connector. It admits the first fact or gives permission for an action, but immediately follows with a restriction, a command, or a more important consideration in the second clause.

sentenceExamples.en: Enjoy your freedom, but you must take responsibility.
Study hard, but don't forget to rest as well.

sentenceExamples.kr: 지원은 해 주되 간섭은 하지 않는 것이 원칙입니다.
sentenceExamples.en: The principle is to provide support but not to interfere.

name: V-노라면
englishMeaning: If you keep doing V... / While V-ing...
briefDescription: A poetic/literary conditional describing a discovery made through continuous action. Similar to: -다 보면 (No. 165).
featuredExample: 옛 사진을 보고 있노라면 어린 시절이 생각나요.
featuredTranslation: If I stay looking at old photos, I am reminded of my childhood.
longerExplanation: Found in songs, poems, and descriptive essays. It suggests that by being in the middle of a continuous state or action, a certain feeling or realization naturally flows in.

sentenceExamples.en: While looking at the river water, my heart becomes peaceful.

sentenceExamples.kr: 열심히 살다 노라면 언젠가는 좋은 날이 오겠죠.
sentenceExamples.en: If you keep living hard, a good day will surely come eventually.

sentenceExamples.kr: 노래를 듣고 있노라면 슬픈 감정이 밀려와요.
sentenceExamples.en: While listening to the song, sad feelings wash over me.

name: N은/는 A/V-(으)ㅁ을 말해 주다
briefDescription: Used to explain the meaning or implication of a specific fact or phenomenon.
featuredExample: 이 지표는 경제가 회복되고 있음을 말해 줍니다.
featuredTranslation: This indicator tells us that the economy is recovering.
longerExplanation: A formal way to interpret data or signs. It presents a noun (N) as evidence and explains what truth or state (nominalized clause) that evidence proves.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그녀의 눈물은 그동안 힘들었음을 말해 주었어요.
sentenceExamples.en: Her tears told us that she had been having a hard time.

sentenceExamples.kr: 이 유적은 당시 문화가 화려했음을 말해 준다.
sentenceExamples.en: These ruins tell us that the culture of that time was magnificent.

sentenceExamples.kr: 낮은 출산율은 사회적 불안이 심각함을 말해 줍니다.
sentenceExamples.en: The low birth rate tells us that social anxiety is serious.

name: N에 대한 논란이 있다
briefDescription: A standard phrase used to introduce a hot topic or a debated subject in news and essays.
featuredExample: 최근 원자력 발전소 건설에 대한 논란이 있습니다.
featuredTranslation: Recently, there is controversy over the construction of nuclear power plants.
longerExplanation: Essential for TOPIK II Task 54 (Writing) or discussions. It objectively introduces a topic that has conflicting opinions in society.

sentenceExamples.kr: 인공지능의 윤리적 가이드라인에 대한 논란이 여전해요.
sentenceExamples.en: Controversy over ethical guidelines for AI still remains.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그 정치인의 발언에 대한 논란이 확산되고 있습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Controversy over that politician's remarks is spreading.

sentenceExamples.kr: 새로운 교육 정책에 대한 논란이 끊이지 않고 있어요.
sentenceExamples.en: Controversy over the new education policy is unceasing.

name: A/V-다는 지적이 있다
englishMeaning: It is pointed out that... / There are criticisms that...
briefDescription: Used to mention a specific criticism or a problem raised by others (experts/public).
featuredExample: 이 정책이 대기업에만 유리하다는 지적이 있습니다.
featuredTranslation: There are points being made that this policy is only advantageous to large corporations.
longerExplanation: A formal way to present a counter-argument or a negative observation without sounding like it is only the speaker's personal opinion. It attributes the point to general observation or experts.

sentenceExamples.kr: 준비가 너무 부족했다는 지적이 나오고 있어요.
sentenceExamples.en: Criticisms are emerging that the preparation was far too insufficient.

sentenceExamples.kr: 현실을 제대로 반영하지 못한다는 지적이 많습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: There are many points being made that it fails to properly reflect reality.
It will be hard to avoid the criticism that it is excessively commercial.

name: A/V-다는 점을 인정하다
briefDescription: Used in debates to acknowledge an opponent's point or a general truth before continuing.
featuredTranslation: They admitted that there was a mistake and apologized.
longerExplanation: A logical tool for argumentation. It shows the speaker is being objective by accepting a certain fact before moving on to their next argument.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그의 주장이 타당하다는 점을 인정하지 않을 수 없어요.
sentenceExamples.en: I cannot help but admit that his argument is valid.

sentenceExamples.kr: 기술의 편리함이 크다는 점을 인정하면서도 부작용이 걱정돼요.
sentenceExamples.en: While admitting that technology is very convenient, I worry about side effects.

sentenceExamples.kr: 우리가 뒤처져 있다는 점을 인정하고 노력해야 합니다.
sentenceExamples.en: We must admit the fact that we are falling behind and work hard.

name: N은/는 물론이려니와
englishMeaning: Not to mention N / Not only N but also...
briefDescription: A stronger variant of -은 물론이고 (No. 306). Used for formal emphasis.
featuredTranslation: Not to mention health, economic power is also important.
longerExplanation: A formal, high-literary additive connector. It emphasizes that the first noun is a given (obvious), and the second noun is equally or more important.

sentenceExamples.en: They are a talented person who possesses character, not to mention skills.

sentenceExamples.kr: 한국은 물론이려니와 전 세계적으로 인기가 많아요.
sentenceExamples.en: It's popular worldwide, not to mention in Korea.

sentenceExamples.kr: 이론은 물론이려니와 실기 실력도 아주 뛰어납니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Their practical skills are outstanding, not to mention their theory.

name: V-는 추세이다
englishMeaning: To be the current trend / To be a growing tendency
briefDescription: Used to describe a social or economic direction that is currently happening.
featuredTranslation: These days, single-person households are a growing trend.
longerExplanation: Used in news and reports to analyze social changes. It describes a movement that has been happening for a while and is expected to continue.

sentenceExamples.kr: 친환경 제품을 선호하는 소비자가 늘고 있는 추세예요.
sentenceExamples.en: Consumers who prefer eco-friendly products are on a growing trend.
I'm worried because prices are on a continuing upward trend.
The number of companies introducing remote work is a growing tendency.

name: A/V-았으면/었으면 하다
englishMeaning: I would like it if... / I wish for...
briefDescription: A softer, more polite way to express a desire or wish. Similar to: -았으면 좋겠다 (No. 3).
featuredTranslation: I would like to just rest well on the weekend.
longerExplanation: While '-았으면 좋겠다' sounds like a direct hope, '-았으면 하다' sounds more like a personal thought or a humble request. It is often used when suggesting something to a superior or expressing a delicate wish.

sentenceExamples.kr: 다 같이 행복하게 지냈으면 하는 마음입니다.
sentenceExamples.en: It is my heart's wish that we all live happily together.
I would like it if you made the decision just a bit more carefully.
I wish (would like it if) this matter is resolved well.

name: A/V-건 (A/V-건) (간에)
englishMeaning: Whether X or Y / Regardless of
briefDescription: Used to show that a certain fact or result remains the same regardless of which option is chosen. Similar to: -든지 (No. 116).
featuredExample: 비가 오건 눈이 오건 간에 우리는 내일 출발할 거예요.
featuredTranslation: Whether it rains or snows, we are leaving tomorrow.
longerExplanation: A formal and literary version of '-든지'. It lists two contrasting options (often opposites like good/bad, go/stay) to emphasize that the final outcome is not affected by these conditions. '간에' is optional but often added for emphasis.

sentenceExamples.en: Whether you succeed or fail, the result isn't important.

sentenceExamples.kr: 누가 뭐라고 하건 간에 제 소신대로 하겠습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: No matter what anyone says, I will act according to my convictions.
Whether the food is tasty or not, the sincerity is what matters.

name: A/V-거니와
briefDescription: Used to connect two related facts where the second reinforces the first. Similar to: -(으)ㄹ 뿐만 아니라 (No. 103).
featuredTranslation: He not only has great skills but also a great personality.
longerExplanation: A high-level formal connector used primarily in writing or formal speeches. It adds a second positive or negative fact to the first one. It sounds more objective and authoritative than the standard '-고' or '-아서/어서'.

sentenceExamples.kr: 날씨가 춥거니와 바람까지 불어서 외출이 힘들어요.
sentenceExamples.en: The weather is cold, and furthermore, it's windy, making it hard to go out.

sentenceExamples.kr: 가격도 저렴하거니와 품질도 뛰어나서 인기가 많습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: It's popular because the price is low and the quality is outstanding.
He is an honest person as well as one with a strong sense of responsibility.

name: A/V-다손 치더라도
englishMeaning: Even if we grant that... / Even assuming that...
briefDescription: Used to acknowledge a hypothetical situation but state it wouldn't change the main point. Similar to: -다 해도 (No. 114).
featuredExample: 아무리 바쁘다손 치더라도 식사는 꼭 하세요.
featuredTranslation: Even granting that you are very busy, make sure to eat.
longerExplanation: A highly formal concessive pattern used in debates. It allows the speaker to 'give in' to an opponent's point temporarily ('even if I agree that X is true') before asserting their own argument as more important.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그 소문이 사실이다손 치더라도 그렇게 화를 낼 일은 아니에요.
sentenceExamples.en: Even assuming that rumor is true, it's not something to get that angry about.

sentenceExamples.kr: 실패한다손 치더라도 도전하는 것 자체에 의미가 있습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Even if we assume failure, there is meaning in the challenge itself.

sentenceExamples.kr: 돈이 많다손 치더라도 건강이 없으면 소용이 없지요.
sentenceExamples.en: Even if one has a lot of money, it's useless without health.

name: N은/는 말할 것도 없다
englishMeaning: It goes without saying that N / Needless to say...
briefDescription: Used to mention a fact that is so obvious it doesn't need explanation. Similar to: -은 물론이고 (No. 306).
featuredExample: 그는 실력은 말할 것도 없고 인성까지 완벽해요.
featuredTranslation: Needless to say he has the skills, his character is even perfect.
longerExplanation: A formal idiomatic expression. It implies 'Why even discuss [N]? It's a clear fact.' It is used to quickly establish a consensus before moving to a secondary point that the speaker wants to highlight.

sentenceExamples.kr: 가족은 말할 것도 없고 친구들도 다 응원하고 있어요.
sentenceExamples.en: It goes without saying that my family is supporting me, but all my friends are too.

sentenceExamples.kr: 서울은 말할 것도 없고 전국적으로 비가 내리고 있습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Needless to say it's raining in Seoul, it's raining nationwide.

sentenceExamples.kr: 이 책은 스토리는 말할 것도 없고 그림이 정말 아름다워요.
sentenceExamples.en: Needless to say the story is good, the illustrations are truly beautiful.

name: V-(으)려고 들다
englishMeaning: To be determined to V / To set one's mind to V (often aggressively)
briefDescription: Describes someone acting with a very strong, often stubborn or intense intention.
featuredExample: 그는 어떻게든 이기려고 들어서 대화가 안 돼요.
featuredTranslation: He's so determined to win that conversation is impossible.
longerExplanation: The verb '들다' adds a nuance of 'plunging into' or 'attacking' an action. It is often used to describe someone who is pushing too hard for a goal or acting based on a strong, singular motivation.

sentenceExamples.kr: 아이가 장난감을 다 가지려고 들어서 걱정이에요.
sentenceExamples.en: I'm worried because the child is determined to have all the toys.

sentenceExamples.kr: 잘못을 감추려고 들면 나중에 더 큰 문제가 됩니다.
sentenceExamples.en: If you set your mind to hiding a mistake, it will become a bigger problem later.

sentenceExamples.kr: 모든 일을 혼자서 다 해내려고 들지 마세요.
sentenceExamples.en: Don't try (be so determined) to do everything all by yourself.

name: A/V-(으)리라
briefDescription: A formal/literary ending expressing a strong future guess or the speaker's firm will.
featuredTranslation: I believe that if you work hard, you will surely succeed.
longerExplanation: Found in classic literature, speeches, and formal resolutions. It is a more 'authoritative' and poetic version of '-(으)ㄹ 것이다'. It sounds like a prophecy or a deep inner conviction.

sentenceExamples.en: When that day comes, everyone shall rejoice.

sentenceExamples.kr: 다시는 이런 실수를 하지 않으리라 결심했어요.
sentenceExamples.en: I resolved that I will never make this kind of mistake again.
I think that someday the truth will be revealed.

name: V-자
briefDescription: Indicates that the action in the second clause happens immediately after the first. Similar to: -자마자 (No. 98).
featuredTranslation: As soon as I arrived home, I made a call.
longerExplanation: A concise, formal version of '-자마자'. It is frequently used in news headlines and historical narratives to show a quick succession of events. Unlike '-자마자', it is more often used in written contexts.

sentenceExamples.en: As soon as class ended, the students went outside.
Right after the rain stopped, a rainbow appeared.
As soon as I heard that news, tears poured out.

name: N(으)로 보다
englishMeaning: To view as N / To regard as N
briefDescription: Used to express a perspective or a standard of judgment.
featuredExample: 저는 이 문제를 기회로 보고 있습니다.
featuredTranslation: I am viewing this problem as an opportunity.
longerExplanation: Used when analyzing a situation or person. It defines the 'lens' through which the subject is interpreted. It is a formal way to state an opinion (e.g., 'I see this as a success').

sentenceExamples.kr: 많은 학자들이 이 현상을 긍정적으로 보고 있어요.
sentenceExamples.en: Many scholars are viewing this phenomenon positively.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그 사건을 단순한 실수로 보기는 어렵습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: It's hard to regard that incident as a simple mistake.

sentenceExamples.kr: 실패를 성공의 과정으로 보는 태도가 필요해요.
sentenceExamples.en: An attitude of viewing failure as a process of success is necessary.

name: A-(으)ㄴ/V-는 가운데
briefDescription: Describes the background state or ongoing situation while something else happens. Similar to: -는 중에.
featuredTranslation: Thank you for attending amidst your busy schedule.
longerExplanation: A formal way to set the scene. It describes a 'surrounding atmosphere' or a 'simultaneous condition.' It is very common in official greetings, news reports, and formal event openings.

sentenceExamples.kr: 폭우가 내리는 가운데 구조 작업이 진행되었습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Rescue operations were carried out amidst heavy rain.

sentenceExamples.kr: 경기가 안 좋은 가운데 물가만 오르고 있어요.
sentenceExamples.en: While the economy is bad (amidst a bad economy), only prices are rising.
The results were announced amidst everyone being tense.

name: V-(으)ㄹ래야 V-(으)ㄹ 수(가) 없다
englishMeaning: Even if I want to V, I cannot / Impossible to V
briefDescription: A strong, emphatic expression of total inability to do an action.
featuredExample: 너무 시끄러워서 집중할래야 할 수가 없어요.
featuredTranslation: It's so noisy that even if I want to concentrate, I absolutely cannot.
longerExplanation: This repeats the verb to emphasize that the speaker's 'will' (intent to do V) is being completely blocked by circumstances. It sounds more frustrated and definitive than a simple '할 수 없다'.

sentenceExamples.kr: 돈이 없어서 그 옷은 살래야 살 수가 없네요.
sentenceExamples.en: I have no money, so even if I wanted to buy those clothes, I just can't.

sentenceExamples.kr: 시간이 부족해서 다 끝낼래야 끝낼 수가 없었습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Time was so short that I couldn't finish it all even if I tried.

sentenceExamples.kr: 너무 닮아서 구별할래야 할 수가 없더라고요.
sentenceExamples.en: They look so much alike that I couldn't distinguish them even if I wanted to.

name: 어찌나 A/V-던지
englishMeaning: It was so A/V that... (Past emphasis)
briefDescription: Used to recall and emphasize the extreme degree of a past state. Similar to: 어찌나 -는지 (No. 252).
featuredExample: 어제는 어찌나 춥던지 얼어 죽는 줄 알았어요.
featuredTranslation: It was so cold yesterday that I thought I was going to freeze to death.
longerExplanation: The combination of '어찌나' and '-던지' creates a strong retrospective exclamation. The speaker is looking back at a past scene and describing how overwhelming or surprising the intensity of that moment was.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그 영화가 어찌나 슬프던지 엉엉 울고 말았어요.
sentenceExamples.en: That movie was so sad that I ended up crying my eyes out.

sentenceExamples.kr: 아이가 어찌나 잘 먹던지 보기만 해도 배가 불렀어요.
sentenceExamples.en: The child ate so well that I felt full just watching.

sentenceExamples.kr: 어찌나 길이 막히던지 평소보다 2시간이나 더 걸렸어요.
sentenceExamples.en: The traffic was so bad that it took two hours longer than usual.

name: A-(으)ㄴ/V-는 데(에) 반해
briefDescription: Used to strongly contrast two different facts or situations. Similar to: -는 반면에 (No. 112).
featuredExample: 형은 공부를 좋아하는 데 반해 동생은 운동을 좋아해요.
featuredTranslation: Whereas the older brother likes studying, the younger brother likes sports.
longerExplanation: A formal contrastive connector. It is often used in comparative analysis or essays to highlight a sharp difference between two subjects or two time periods.

sentenceExamples.kr: 물가는 비싼 데 반해 소득은 제자리걸음입니다.
sentenceExamples.en: While prices are expensive, income is at a standstill.

sentenceExamples.kr: 수출은 증가한 데 반해 내수 시장은 여전히 침체되어 있어요.
sentenceExamples.en: In contrast to exports increasing, the domestic market is still stagnant.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그는 겉은 차가운 데 반해 속은 아주 따뜻한 사람이에요.
sentenceExamples.en: Whereas he looks cold on the outside, he is a very warm person inside.

name: V-(으)ㅁ에 따라
englishMeaning: As V happens... / In accordance with V...
briefDescription: Shows that one result changes or happens as a direct consequence of an action's progress. Similar to: -아/어감에 따라.
featuredExample: 기술이 발전함에 따라 우리의 삶도 변하고 있습니다.
featuredTranslation: As technology develops, our lives are also changing.
longerExplanation: Used in formal logic to show a proportional change. As Action A progresses or develops, Situation B follows that same trajectory. It is standard for scientific and sociological reporting.

sentenceExamples.kr: 인구가 고령화됨에 따라 새로운 사회 문제가 발생하고 있어요.
sentenceExamples.en: As the population ages, new social problems are occurring.

sentenceExamples.kr: 시간이 흐름에 따라 오해도 서서히 풀리기 마련입니다.
sentenceExamples.en: As time flows, it's natural that misunderstandings gradually resolve.

sentenceExamples.kr: 경제 상황이 변함에 따라 투자 전략도 달라져야 합니다.
sentenceExamples.en: As the economic situation changes, investment strategies must also vary.

name: V-(으)ㄹ 바에는 [바에야] (차라리)
englishMeaning: Rather than V / If you're going to V anyway
briefDescription: Used when choosing a better option among poor choices. Similar to: -느니 차라리 (No. 169).
featuredExample: 그렇게 대충 할 바에는 차라리 시작을 하지 마세요.
featuredTranslation: If you're going to do it so half-heartedly, you'd be better off not starting at all.
longerExplanation: This is a strong expression of preference. It acknowledges a situation or choice in the first clause but suggests that if that is the case, an alternative (often an extreme one) is much better. It carries a tone of advice or stern warning.

sentenceExamples.kr: 비싼 돈을 주고 살 바에야 직접 만드는 게 낫겠어요.
sentenceExamples.en: Rather than paying a lot of money to buy it, it would be better to make it myself.

sentenceExamples.kr: 포기할 바에는 죽을 힘을 다해 노력해 보겠어.
sentenceExamples.en: Rather than giving up, I will try with all my might.

sentenceExamples.kr: 지각해서 혼날 바에야 아예 안 가는 게 나을지도 몰라.
sentenceExamples.en: If I'm going to get in trouble for being late anyway, it might be better not to go at all.

name: A-(으)ㄴ/V-는 까닭에 [까닭으로]
briefDescription: A highly formal and literary way to state a reason. Similar to: -기 때문에 (No. 26).
featuredExample: 준비가 부족했던 까닭에 사고를 막지 못했습니다.
featuredTranslation: Because the preparation was insufficient, the accident could not be prevented.
longerExplanation: '까닭' is a formal noun meaning 'reason' or 'cause.' Using this structure makes the sentence sound very objective and analytical. It is common in history books, formal reports, and news editorials.

sentenceExamples.kr: 날씨가 험악한 까닭에 배가 출항하지 못하고 있어요.
sentenceExamples.en: For the reason that the weather is harsh, the ship is unable to set sail.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그가 정직하지 못한 까닭으로 신뢰를 잃고 말았습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Because he was not honest, he ended up losing everyone's trust.

sentenceExamples.kr: 경기가 침체된 까닭에 소비가 위축되고 있습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Due to the economic recession, consumption is shrinking.

name: A/V-다 뿐이지
englishMeaning: It's just that... / The only difference is...
briefDescription: Used to show that two things are essentially the same, with only a minor or specific difference.
featuredExample: 이름만 다르다 뿐이지 사실상 같은 제품이에요.
featuredTranslation: The only difference is the name; it's practically the same product.
longerExplanation: This pattern emphasizes that Action A and Action B (or State A and B) are equivalent in essence. It highlights that the only 'remaining' factor is the one mentioned in the first clause.

sentenceExamples.kr: 말을 안 한다 뿐이지 속으로는 다 알고 있을 거야.
sentenceExamples.en: It's just that they aren't speaking; they likely know everything inside.

sentenceExamples.kr: 시간이 좀 걸린다 뿐이지 누구나 할 수 있는 일입니다.
sentenceExamples.en: The only thing is that it takes some time; it's work anyone can do.

sentenceExamples.kr: 표현 방식이 다르다 뿐이지 두 사람의 생각은 같습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: It's just that their ways of expression are different; their thoughts are the same.

name: V-기란
englishMeaning: As for doing V / The act of V-ing is...
briefDescription: Used to emphasize a verb as the subject of a sentence, often describing it as difficult. Similar to: V-는 것은.
featuredExample: 매일 꾸준히 운동하기란 쉽지 않은 일이에요.
featuredTranslation: As for exercising steadily every day, it is no easy task.
longerExplanation: This is a contraction of '-기라는 것은'. It singles out a specific action and presents it as a topic for evaluation. It is almost always followed by an adjective describing the difficulty or nature of that action.

sentenceExamples.kr: 외국어로 농담을 하기란 여간 어려운 게 아닙니다.
sentenceExamples.en: As for making jokes in a foreign language, it is extraordinarily difficult.
Admitting failure is a painful process for anyone.

sentenceExamples.kr: 진실을 밝히기란 때로는 용기가 필요한 법입니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Revealing the truth is an act that naturally requires courage sometimes.

name: A/V-(으)ㄹ지라도
briefDescription: A strong concessive connector used for hypothetical or extreme situations. Similar to: -아/어도 (No. 8).
featuredTranslation: No matter how hard it may be, I will never give up.
longerExplanation: A high-level formal version of '-아/어도'. It is used to express a firm resolve or an absolute fact that remains true despite a significant obstacle or a hypothetical 'worst-case' scenario.

sentenceExamples.en: Even if the wind and rain lash down, we must move forward.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그가 나를 배신할지라도 나는 그를 원망하지 않겠다.
sentenceExamples.en: Even if he were to betray me, I would not resent him.

sentenceExamples.kr: 세월이 흐를지라도 우리의 우정은 변하지 않을 거예요.
sentenceExamples.en: Even though time flows, our friendship will not change.

name: V-고서는
englishMeaning: Only after doing V / Unless V happens...
briefDescription: Indicates that the first action is a mandatory prerequisite for the second. Similar to: -고 나서야 (No. 185).
featuredExample: 직접 먹어 보고서는 그 맛을 평가할 수 없어요.
featuredTranslation: Unless you try eating it yourself, you cannot evaluate the taste.
