longerExplanation: Often used in negative sentences to show that without completing the first action, the second state or result is impossible. It stresses the dependency of the result on the preceding action.

sentenceExamples.kr: 범인을 잡고서는 이 사건을 끝낼 수 없습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Unless we catch the culprit, we cannot end this case.

sentenceExamples.kr: 돈을 벌고서는 사고 싶은 걸 다 살 거예요.
sentenceExamples.en: Only after earning money will I buy everything I want.

sentenceExamples.kr: 공부를 하지 않고서는 성공하기 어려운 법입니다.
sentenceExamples.en: It is natural that it's hard to succeed without studying.

name: V-게끔
briefDescription: Indicates a goal or a desired state for an action. Similar to: -게 (No. 22).
featuredExample: 모두가 들을 수 있게끔 크게 말씀해 주세요.
featuredTranslation: Please speak loudly so that everyone can hear.
longerExplanation: Adding '-끔' to the purpose connector '-게' adds a nuance of 'reaching a specific point' or 'ensuring a certain result.' It is often used when giving instructions to achieve a specific outcome.

sentenceExamples.kr: 아이가 잘 수 있게끔 방을 어둡게 해 주세요.
sentenceExamples.en: Make the room dark so that the baby can sleep.

sentenceExamples.kr: 늦지 않게끔 미리 준비하는 것이 좋겠어요.
sentenceExamples.en: It's best to prepare in advance so as not to be late.
I told everything truthfully so that there would be no misunderstanding.

name: A-기(가) 이를 데 없다
englishMeaning: To be incomparably A / To be A beyond words
briefDescription: Used to describe an extreme state, usually a positive one. Similar to: -기 짝이 없다 (No. 301).
featuredExample: 그의 성공 소식은 기쁘기 이를 데 없었습니다.
featuredTranslation: The news of his success was joyful beyond words.
longerExplanation: Literally 'there is no place to reach (the end of A).' While '-기 짝이 없다' is often used for negative states, '-기 이를 데 없다' is frequently used for positive or magnificent descriptions (beauty, joy, honor).

sentenceExamples.kr: 경치가 아름답기 이를 데 없어서 감탄했어요.
sentenceExamples.en: I was in awe because the scenery was incomparably beautiful.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그분의 인품은 훌륭하기 이를 데 없습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: His character is excellent beyond compare.

sentenceExamples.kr: 이런 큰 상을 받게 되어 영광스럽기 이를 데 없네요.
sentenceExamples.en: It is a joy beyond words to receive such a great award.

name: N더러
briefDescription: A particle used when the speaker is quoting a command or request to a specific person. Similar to: N한테/에게.
featuredExample: 엄마가 동생더러 심부름을 갔다 오라고 하셨어요.
featuredTranslation: Mom told my younger sibling to go on an errand.
longerExplanation: Used primarily with verbs of 'saying,' 'asking,' or 'ordering' (말하다, 시키다, 부탁하다). It is informal but very common when relaying instructions directed at a third person.

sentenceExamples.en: Who are you calling a fool?
The teacher told the students to be quiet.
I pestered my friend to go with me.

name: N이/가 다 뭐예요?
englishMeaning: What do you mean N? / N is the least of my worries
briefDescription: Used to dismiss a noun as being irrelevant or insufficient compared to a much larger problem.
featuredExample: 칭찬이 다 뭐예요? 욕만 안 먹으면 다행이죠.
featuredTranslation: What do you mean 'praise'? I'm just lucky I'm not getting insulted.
longerExplanation: A rhetorical question used to show that a certain expectation is far-fetched or trivial given the harsh reality of the current situation. It emphasizes a sense of frustration or a gap between hope and reality.

sentenceExamples.kr: 휴가가 다 뭐예요? 일주일 내내 야근하느라고 정신없어요.
sentenceExamples.en: What do you mean 'vacation'? I'm out of my mind working overtime all week.
What do you mean 'dieting'? I'm starving to death here.
What do you mean 'apology'? I told you it's already too late.

name: N은/는 고사하고
englishMeaning: Let alone N / Setting aside N
briefDescription: Used to say that even a basic or easier thing is impossible. Similar to: -은/는커녕 (No. 109).
featuredExample: 밥은 고사하고 물 한 모금도 못 마셨어요.
featuredTranslation: Let alone a meal, I couldn't even drink a sip of water.
longerExplanation: A formal and emphatic version of '-은/는커녕'. It essentially means that the first noun is a luxury or a high expectation that cannot even be considered because even something much simpler is failing.

sentenceExamples.kr: 칭찬은 고사하고 혼만 나지 않으면 좋겠어요.
sentenceExamples.en: Let alone being praised, I just hope I don't get in trouble.

sentenceExamples.kr: 해외여행은 고사하고 국내 여행 갈 시간도 없어요.
sentenceExamples.en: Let alone traveling abroad, I don't even have time to travel domestically.
Let alone getting married, I don't even have the luxury to date.

name: A/V-든지 A/V-든지 하다
englishMeaning: Either do X or do Y (specifically)
briefDescription: Used to suggest or describe a choice between two actions to resolve a situation. Similar to: -거나 -거나 하다 (No. 331).
featuredTranslation: If you don't know, either ask or look it up in a book.
longerExplanation: While '-든지' (No. 116) usually shows indifference, this full pattern '-든지 -든지 하다' is used to offer a concrete range of solutions or to describe someone's alternating behaviors. It sounds more decisive and instructional.

sentenceExamples.kr: 비가 오면 실내에서 놀든지 영화를 보든지 합시다.
sentenceExamples.en: If it rains, let's either play indoors or watch a movie.

sentenceExamples.kr: 사과를 하든지 해명을 하든지 해야 할 것 같아요.
sentenceExamples.en: You should either apologize or give an explanation.

sentenceExamples.kr: 공부를 하든지 잠을 자든지 하나만 선택해.
sentenceExamples.en: Either study or sleep; just pick one.

name: N와/과 맞먹다
englishMeaning: To be on par with N / To be equal to N
briefDescription: A descriptive phrase used to show that a value or status is equivalent to a high standard.
featuredExample: 이 아파트 가격은 서울 도심의 집값과 맞먹습니다.
featuredTranslation: The price of this apartment is on par with housing prices in downtown Seoul.
longerExplanation: Used when comparing two things to emphasize how great or significant the first one is by equating it to a well-known high standard. Often used in economic contexts regarding prices or capabilities.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그의 실력은 전문가와 맞먹을 정도로 뛰어납니다.
sentenceExamples.en: His skills are outstanding to the point of being on par with an expert.

sentenceExamples.kr: 한 달 월급이 웬만한 자동차 가격과 맞먹네요.
sentenceExamples.en: One month's salary is equal to the price of a decent car.

sentenceExamples.kr: 작은 중소기업의 매출이 대기업과 맞먹는 수준입니다.
sentenceExamples.en: The sales of that small business are at a level equal to a large corporation.

name: 설령 [설사/가령] A/V-다(고) 해도
englishMeaning: Even assuming that... / Even if we suppose...
briefDescription: An emphatic concessive connector for extreme hypothetical situations. Similar to: -다손 치더라도 (No. 352).
featuredExample: 설령 실패한다고 해도 다시 일어설 용기가 있습니다.
featuredTranslation: Even assuming I fail, I have the courage to stand up again.
longerExplanation: This is a formal 'worst-case scenario' conditional. The adverbs '설령' or '설사' add a strong rhetorical weight, implying that even if the most unlikely or negative event were to happen, the speaker's resolve remains unchanged.

sentenceExamples.kr: 설사 그게 사실이라 해도 나는 너를 믿을 거야.
sentenceExamples.en: Even if that were the truth, I would still believe you.

sentenceExamples.kr: 설령 비바람이 칠지라도 우리의 행진은 계속됩니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Even assuming it storms, our march will continue.

sentenceExamples.kr: 가령 지구가 멸망한다 해도 오늘 할 일을 하겠습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Suppose the world ends; I will still do what I must today.

name: V-(으)ㄹ라치면
englishMeaning: Whenever one tries to V / Every time I'm about to V
briefDescription: Used to describe a situation that consistently happens whenever the subject intends to do an action.
featuredExample: 공부를 하려라치면 꼭 친구한테 전화가 와요.
featuredTranslation: Whenever I'm about to start studying, a friend always calls me.
longerExplanation: A conversational but advanced conditional. It focuses on the recurring nature of an obstacle or event that interrupts an intended action. It implies a sense of irony or annoyance.

sentenceExamples.kr: 외출을 하려라치면 갑자기 비가 쏟아지곤 해요.
sentenceExamples.en: Every time I'm about to go out, it suddenly pours with rain.

sentenceExamples.kr: 다이어트를 시작하려라치면 맛있는 게 눈에 띄네요.
sentenceExamples.en: Whenever I try to start a diet, delicious food catches my eye.

sentenceExamples.kr: 책을 좀 읽으려라치면 아이가 울기 시작해요.
sentenceExamples.en: Every time I try to read a book, the baby starts crying.

name: A/V-다고 할 것까지는 [할 것까지야] 없다
englishMeaning: It's not to the extent that one would call it... / Not quite X
briefDescription: Used to downplay a description, saying it doesn't reach a certain extreme label.
featuredExample: 화가 났다고 할 것까지는 없지만 좀 서운하긴 해요.
featuredTranslation: It's not that I'm angry exactly, but I am a bit hurt.
longerExplanation: Used for precise communication. It acknowledges that a situation is close to a certain label (like 'expert' or 'angry') but clarifies that the degree is actually lower or less serious than that word implies.

sentenceExamples.kr: 전문가라고 할 것까지는 없지만 웬만한 건 다 압니다.
sentenceExamples.en: I wouldn't go as far as to call myself an expert, but I know most things.

sentenceExamples.kr: 비싸다고 할 것까지야 없지만 저렴한 편도 아니에요.
sentenceExamples.en: It's not exactly expensive, but it's not cheap either.

sentenceExamples.kr: 성공이라고 할 것까지는 없어도 큰 진전이었습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Even if you can't call it a success yet, it was great progress.

name: A/V-다고 치다
englishMeaning: Let's assume that... / Even if we suppose...
briefDescription: Used to temporarily accept an opponent's premise in an argument. Similar to: -다고 가정하다.
featuredExample: 그 말이 맞다고 치고, 다음 문제는 어떻게 할 거예요?
featuredTranslation: Let's assume you're right; what are you going to do about the next problem?
longerExplanation: A common debate pattern. It allows a speaker to move past a disputed point by 'conceding' it for the sake of the current discussion, usually to point out a different, larger problem.

sentenceExamples.kr: 돈이 많다고 칩시다. 행복은 살 수 있나요?
sentenceExamples.en: Let's say (assume) you have lots of money. Can you buy happiness?

sentenceExamples.kr: 과거는 잊었다고 치고 우리 새로 시작해요.
sentenceExamples.en: Let's assume the past is forgotten and start anew.
Even if we assume it was a mistake, you must take responsibility.

name: V-(으)ㄹ 리 만무하다
englishMeaning: There is absolutely no reason for V / Completely impossible
briefDescription: A highly formal and strongest possible denial of a fact. Similar to: -(으)ㄹ 리가 없다 (No. 96).
featuredExample: 그 정직한 사람이 거짓말을 했을 리 만무합니다.
featuredTranslation: There is absolutely no reason that such an honest person would have lied.
longerExplanation: '만무하다' means 'to not exist at all.' Combining this with '리' (reason) creates an absolute logical wall. It is frequently used in legal judgments, logic-heavy essays, and news analysis.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그 소문이 진실일 리 만무하다는 증거가 나왔어요.
sentenceExamples.en: Evidence has emerged that it's impossible for that rumor to be true.

sentenceExamples.kr: 아무런 노력 없이 성공할 리 만무하지요.
sentenceExamples.en: There is absolutely no way to succeed without any effort.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그가 약속을 잊었을 리 만무하니 조금 더 기다려 봅시다.
sentenceExamples.en: It is completely impossible that he forgot the promise, so let's wait a bit longer.

name: A/V-던 차에 [차이다]
englishMeaning: Just as I was... / At the moment of...
briefDescription: Describes the exact moment an intended action was about to happen or was in progress. Similar to: -(으)려던 참에 (No. 104).
featuredExample: 배가 고프던 차에 친구가 피자를 사 왔어요.
featuredTranslation: Just as I was feeling hungry, my friend bought pizza.
longerExplanation: '차' refers to a specific timing or opportunity. This structure indicates that the situation in the second clause happened exactly when the speaker was in the state or action of the first clause.

sentenceExamples.kr: 은행에 가려던 차에 비가 오기 시작했어요.
sentenceExamples.en: Just as I was about to go to the bank, it started to rain.

sentenceExamples.kr: 심심하던 차에 잘 왔어. 같이 게임하자.
sentenceExamples.en: You came at the perfect time (just as I was bored). Let's play a game.

sentenceExamples.kr: 고민하던 차에 당신의 조언이 큰 도움이 됐습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Your advice was a big help just when I was agonizing over it.

name: A/V-(으)ㄹ 성싶다
englishMeaning: I guess... / It seems likely that...
briefDescription: A literary and slightly archaic-sounding conjecture. Similar to: -(으)ㄹ 것 같다 (No. 1).
featuredTranslation: The weather looks like it might rain tomorrow.
longerExplanation: Found in classic literature or used by older generations to express a thoughtful guess. It sounds more gentle and speculative than the standard '-것 같다.'

sentenceExamples.en: It seems likely that the misunderstanding will finally be resolved.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그의 말이 사실일 성싶어 마음이 놓여요.
sentenceExamples.en: I feel relieved as it seems likely his words are true.
It seems likely that good news will be heard before long.

name: (비록/차라리) A/V-(으)ㄹ지언정
briefDescription: A strong resolve pattern where the subject accepts a hardship but rejects a worse moral choice. Similar to: -ㄹ망정 (No. 309).
featuredTranslation: Although I may be poor, I will not live cowardly.
longerExplanation: This is a grammar of 'pride and principles.' It establishes a difficult but acceptable reality (A) and contrasts it with an unacceptable or shameful reality (B).

sentenceExamples.en: Even if I fail, I will not be someone who doesn't even try.
Even if I die, I cannot reveal the secret.

sentenceExamples.kr: 조금 늦을지언정 정확하게 하는 게 중요해요.
sentenceExamples.en: Although it might be a bit late, doing it accurately is what matters.

name: V-ㄴ/는답시고
englishMeaning: With the intention of doing V (Sarcastic/Negative)
briefDescription: Used to mock or criticize an action that failed or was pretentious. Similar to: -ㄴ/는다고 하면서.
featuredExample: 도와준답시고 한 일이 오히려 방해가 됐어요.
featuredTranslation: The thing he did 'claiming' to be helping actually became a hindrance.
longerExplanation: A judgmental pattern used to describe someone doing something for a 'supposed' reason that the speaker finds annoying, insufficient, or silly.

sentenceExamples.en: Claiming to be cooking, he's left the kitchen in a complete mess.
I saw him just sitting at the desk, claiming to be studying (but not actually doing it).

sentenceExamples.kr: 효도한답시고 준 것이 다 깨진 그릇이었어요.
sentenceExamples.en: The thing he gave 'as an act of filial piety' was a broken bowl.

name: A/V-(으)ㄹ 턱이 없다
englishMeaning: No way... / There's no reason that...
briefDescription: Strong disbelief based on common sense. Similar to: -(으)ㄹ 리가 없다 (No. 96).
featuredExample: 그가 거짓말을 할 턱이 없는데 이상하네요.
featuredTranslation: There's no way he would lie; it's strange.
longerExplanation: '턱' refers to a logical ground or reason. This is a conversational but firm way to say that something is impossible because it doesn't make logical sense.

sentenceExamples.kr: 어린아이가 이걸 다 먹었을 턱이 없지.
sentenceExamples.en: There's no way a small child ate all of this.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그렇게 비싼 옷을 제가 살 턱이 있겠어요?
sentenceExamples.en: Is there any way I would buy such expensive clothes? (No way).

sentenceExamples.kr: 약속을 잊었을 턱이 없어요. 어제도 통화했거든요.
sentenceExamples.en: There's no way he forgot; we spoke on the phone yesterday.

name: N(으)로 말미암아
englishMeaning: Due to N / Caused by N (Formal)
briefDescription: A highly formal, literary way to state a cause. Similar to: -로 인해서 (No. 310 similar).
featuredExample: 작은 부주의로 말미암아 큰 사고가 났습니다.
featuredTranslation: A major accident occurred due to a small moment of carelessness.
longerExplanation: Found in historical texts or formal news reporting. It connects a specific noun to a significant consequence, often a negative or large-scale one.

sentenceExamples.en: Countless refugees were created due to the war.

sentenceExamples.kr: 신기술 개발로 말미암아 인류의 삶이 변했습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Human life has changed due to the development of new technology.

sentenceExamples.kr: 오해로 말미암아 두 사람의 관계가 멀어졌어요.
sentenceExamples.en: The relationship between the two became distant due to a misunderstanding.

name: N에 지나지 않다
englishMeaning: To be nothing more than N / Merely N
briefDescription: Used to downplay the importance or scale of something. Similar to: N에 불과하다 (No. 273).
featuredExample: 이것은 시작에 지나지 않으니 너무 기뻐하지 마세요.
featuredTranslation: This is nothing more than the beginning, so don't be too happy.
longerExplanation: A formal and cool-headed expression. It suggests that while something might look big or important, its actual value or progress is limited to the noun mentioned.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그 소문은 뜬구름 잡는 이야기에 지나지 않습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: That rumor is nothing more than an unrealistic story.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그는 내 인생의 한 조각에 지나지 않아요.
sentenceExamples.en: He is nothing more than a small piece of my life.
Because there were merely 10 participants, the event was canceled.

name: A/V-기로서니
englishMeaning: Even if it is the case that... / No matter how...
briefDescription: Used to acknowledge a fact but argue it is no excuse for a certain behavior. Similar to: -다고 해도.
featuredExample: 아무리 돈이 없기로서니 도둑질을 해서야 되겠어요?
featuredTranslation: No matter how little money you have, is it okay to steal?
longerExplanation: This is a rhetorical concessive connector. The speaker admits the first clause is true but finds the second clause's reaction or result to be unacceptable or surprising. It often ends with a rhetorical question like '-겠어요?' or '-나?'.

sentenceExamples.kr: 배가 고프기로서니 남의 음식을 함부로 먹으면 안 되지.
sentenceExamples.en: Even if you were hungry, you shouldn't just eat someone else's food.

sentenceExamples.kr: 아무리 바쁘기로서니 부모님 생신을 잊을 수 있니?
sentenceExamples.en: No matter how busy you are, how could you forget your parents' birthday?
Even if you failed the exam, should you be that discouraged?

name: V-아/어 주십사 (하고)
englishMeaning: Requesting that you please do V / Humbling asking for V
briefDescription: A highly formal and humble way to make a request to a superior or organization.
featuredExample: 부디 너그러운 마음으로 용서해 주십사 하고 찾아왔습니다.
featuredTranslation: I have come humbly requesting that you please forgive me with a generous heart.
longerExplanation: This is an extremely formal honorific request, far above '-아/어 주세요.' It is typically used in formal letters, petitions, or when a person in a much lower status addresses a person of high authority to ask for a favor or reconsideration.

sentenceExamples.kr: 사업 계획을 재고해 주십사 하고 메일을 드립니다.
sentenceExamples.en: I am emailing you humbly requesting that you please reconsider the business plan.

sentenceExamples.kr: 한 번만 더 기회를 주십사 하고 간곡히 부탁드렸어요.
sentenceExamples.en: I earnestly requested that they please give me one more chance.

sentenceExamples.kr: 행사에 참석해 주십사 하고 직접 방문했습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: I came in person humbly requesting that you please attend the event.

name: N인지라
englishMeaning: Because it is N / Given that it is N
briefDescription: A formal and literary way to state a reason based on a noun's nature. Similar to: N이라서 (No. 78).
featuredExample: 초행길인지라 길을 찾는 데 한참 걸렸어요.
featuredTranslation: Given that it was my first time on this road, it took a long while to find the way.
longerExplanation: Used primarily in written style or formal storytelling. It suggests that the reason for the following situation is an unavoidable or natural characteristic of the noun mentioned. It carries an 'as might be expected' nuance.

sentenceExamples.kr: 워낙 대공사인지라 완공까지 시간이 오래 걸릴 법해요.
sentenceExamples.en: Since it is such a large-scale construction, it's likely to take a long time to complete.
Given that it's a holiday, the highway is very crowded.
Because I was the youngest, I grew up receiving all the affection at home.

name: 어디 N뿐인가(요)?
englishMeaning: Is it only N? / It's much more than just N
briefDescription: A rhetorical question used to show that there are many more examples besides N.
featuredExample: 그가 잘하는 게 어디 노래뿐인가요? 춤도 잘 춰요.
featuredTranslation: Is singing the only thing he's good at? He dances well too.
longerExplanation: This phrase is used for emphasis. It suggests that 'N' is just the starting point of a long list of characteristics or facts. It translates to 'N is not the only thing; there is also...' or 'Don't even get me started on N.'

sentenceExamples.kr: 환경 오염의 원인이 어디 플라스틱뿐인가요? 비닐도 큰 문제죠.
sentenceExamples.en: Is plastic the only cause of environmental pollution? Vinyl is also a major problem.

sentenceExamples.kr: 서울의 명소가 어디 남산뿐인가요? 갈 곳이 정말 많아요.
sentenceExamples.en: Is Namsan the only famous spot in Seoul? There are so many places to go.

sentenceExamples.kr: 이 책의 장점이 어디 스토리뿐인가요? 교훈도 아주 깊습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Is the story the only merit of this book? The lesson is also very deep.

name: V-느니만 못하다
englishMeaning: To be not as good as... / To be worse than...
briefDescription: Used to say that a certain action is actually worse than an alternative. Similar to: N만 못하다 (No. 274).
featuredExample: 대충 할 바에는 안 하느니만 못해요.
featuredTranslation: If you're going to do it half-heartedly, it's not even as good as (worse than) not doing it at all.
longerExplanation: This structure compares an action (V) with its negative or a different baseline. It implies that the current action is a waste of time or effort and that 'not doing it' would actually be a better outcome.

sentenceExamples.en: Making mistakes by rushing is worse than (not as good as) doing it slowly.

sentenceExamples.kr: 맛없는 걸 억지로 먹느니 차라리 굶느니만 못해요.
sentenceExamples.en: Eating something untasty by force is worse than just starving.

sentenceExamples.kr: 거짓말로 위기만 모면하는 것은 진실을 밝히느니만 못하다.
sentenceExamples.en: Escaping a crisis with a lie is not as good as revealing the truth.

name: V-아/어 봤자 [봤댔자]
englishMeaning: Even if you try V / No use V-ing
briefDescription: Expresses the futility of an action. Similar to: -아/어 봐야 (No. 100).
featuredTranslation: Even if you regret it now, it's already too late (no use).
longerExplanation: A conversational but advanced version of '-아/어 봐야'. It emphasizes that the effort in the first clause will result in no change or a negative result. '봤댔자' is an even more emphatic/cynical spoken variant.

sentenceExamples.kr: 아무리 설명해 봤자 그 사람은 이해 못 할 거예요.
sentenceExamples.en: No matter how much you try to explain, that person won't understand.

sentenceExamples.kr: 뛰어 봤자 벼룩이지 얼마나 멀리 가겠어?
sentenceExamples.en: A flea is still just a flea even if it jumps; how far could it go? (Proverb meaning you can't escape your limits).

sentenceExamples.kr: 소리를 질러 봤자 아무도 안 도와줘요.
sentenceExamples.en: Even if you scream, no one will help you.

name: V-(으)랴 V-(으)랴
englishMeaning: Busy doing X and also Y / Juggling X and Y
briefDescription: Used to describe a very busy or hectic situation where one must handle two things at once.
featuredExample: 낮에는 일하랴 밤에는 공부하랴 눈코 뜰 새 없이 바빠요.
featuredTranslation: Between working during the day and studying at night, I'm incredibly busy.
longerExplanation: This pattern lists two demanding tasks to emphasize the difficulty or the effort required to manage both. It creates a sense of being 'pulled in two directions' or being overwhelmed by responsibilities.

sentenceExamples.kr: 아이 키우랴 직장 다니랴 정신이 하나도 없어요.
sentenceExamples.en: Juggling raising a child and going to work, I'm completely out of my mind.

sentenceExamples.kr: 손님 맞으랴 음식 준비하랴 정말 고생 많으셨네요.
sentenceExamples.en: You really went through a lot, between welcoming guests and preparing food.

sentenceExamples.kr: 돈 벌랴 집안일 하랴 몸이 열 개라도 모자랄 지경이에요.
sentenceExamples.en: Between earning money and doing housework, I'm at the point where even ten bodies wouldn't be enough.

name: V-(으)ㄹ세라
briefDescription: Used when the subject does an action because they are afraid of a certain outcome. Similar to: -(으)ㄹ까 봐 (No. 95).
featuredTranslation: Lest someone see, I quickly put it in my pocket.
longerExplanation: A literary and slightly poetic pattern. It describes an action taken out of a sense of caution or anxiety that something negative might happen. It is often found in novels or descriptive prose.

sentenceExamples.kr: 아이가 잠에서 깰세라 조심스럽게 문을 닫았습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Fearing the baby might wake up, I closed the door carefully.
Lest I miss the opportunity, I hurried to submit the application.
Fearing that rumors might spread, I didn't tell anyone.

name: N을/를 불문하고
englishMeaning: Regardless of N / Irrespective of N
briefDescription: Similar to -을 막론하고 (No. 305); indicates that N is not a factor.
featuredExample: 이유 여하를 불문하고 약속은 지켜야 합니다.
featuredTranslation: Regardless of the reason, promises must be kept.
longerExplanation: Used in formal logic to show that a statement is universally applicable across all categories of the noun mentioned. '불문(不問)' literally means 'not asking.'

sentenceExamples.en: Irrespective of time or place, honesty is the best value.

sentenceExamples.kr: 국적을 불문하고 누구나 참여할 수 있습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Anyone can participate regardless of nationality.

sentenceExamples.kr: 남녀노소를 불문하고 그 가수는 인기가 많아요.
sentenceExamples.en: That singer is popular regardless of age or gender.

name: V-(으)ㄴ/는 이상
briefDescription: Used when a certain fact or decision is established, making the next action inevitable. Similar to: -(으)니까 (No. 20).
featuredExample: 이미 약속한 이상 반드시 지켜야 해요.
featuredTranslation: Now that I've already promised, I must keep it.
longerExplanation: This is a 'logic of necessity.' It indicates that because a certain threshold has been crossed or a choice has been made, there is a natural responsibility or unavoidable outcome that must follow.

sentenceExamples.en: Since I've started, I must see it through to the end.

sentenceExamples.kr: 한국에 온 이상 한국말을 완벽하게 배우고 싶어요.
sentenceExamples.en: Now that I've come to Korea, I want to learn Korean perfectly.

sentenceExamples.kr: 범인임이 밝혀진 이상 처벌을 피할 수 없을 거예요.
sentenceExamples.en: Since it's been revealed they are the culprit, they won't be able to avoid punishment.

name: A/V-(으)니/느니 A/V-(으)니/느니 (하다)
englishMeaning: Saying this and that / Complaining about X and Y
briefDescription: Used to describe people making various excuses or comments. Similar to: -니 -니 하다 (No. 335).
featuredTranslation: They're just grumbling, saying it's expensive or that it's untasty.
longerExplanation: This pattern captures a scene of nitpicking or listing various opinions. It often carries a negative nuance, describing someone who is being difficult, indecisive, or annoying with their words.

sentenceExamples.kr: 좋으니 싫으니 해도 결국은 살 거잖아.
sentenceExamples.en: Whether you say you like it or hate it, you're going to buy it anyway.
They hesitated for a long time, saying they would go or not go.

sentenceExamples.kr: 시간이 없느니 돈이 없느니 핑계 대지 마세요.
sentenceExamples.en: Don't make excuses, saying you have no time or no money.

name: A/V-건만
briefDescription: A literary and formal version of -지만. Similar to: -건마는.
featuredExample: 달은 밝건만 내 마음은 어둡기만 하구나.
featuredTranslation: The moon is bright, yet my heart is only dark.
longerExplanation: Found in poems, song lyrics, and high-level novels. It is a more evocative and emotional way to show contrast. It often carries a tone of lament or deep reflection on a contradiction.

sentenceExamples.en: Time flows, yet the memory is still vivid.

sentenceExamples.kr: 꽃은 피건만 봄은 아직 오지 않은 듯합니다.
sentenceExamples.en: The flowers are blooming, yet it appears spring hasn't truly come.
I worked hard, but the result was not good.

name: V-는 게 고작이다
englishMeaning: All one can do is V / To be only V-ing (limited)
briefDescription: Used to show that a result is at a very low level despite effort.
featuredExample: 하루 종일 일했지만 겨우 한 페이지를 쓴 게 고작이에요.
featuredTranslation: I worked all day, but all I managed to do was write a single page.
longerExplanation: '고작' means 'at most' or 'only.' This grammar expresses the speaker's frustration that the final outcome of a significant effort was very small or limited. It emphasizes a lack of achievement.

sentenceExamples.kr: 월급을 받아도 방세를 내는 게 고작입니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Even if I get paid, paying the rent is the best I can do (it's the limit).

sentenceExamples.kr: 집에서 쉬는 날에는 티비만 보는 게 고작이에요.
sentenceExamples.en: On my rest days, watching TV is all I ever manage to do.

sentenceExamples.kr: 도와준다는 게 옆에서 쳐다보는 게 고작이네요.
sentenceExamples.en: Your 'helping' is merely watching from the side (that's the extent of it).

name: N(이)며 N(이)며
englishMeaning: N and N / Both N and N
briefDescription: Used to list multiple nouns emphatically to show that everything in a category is included. Similar to: N하고 N (No. 48).
featuredExample: 그는 외모며 성격이며 빠지는 게 하나도 없어요.
featuredTranslation: He has everything, from looks to personality; nothing is lacking.
longerExplanation: Introduced in SNU Book 4. It is used to enumerate nouns to show that they are all relevant. It is more descriptive and formal than '하고' or '랑'. It often implies a sense of 'all of these things combined.'

sentenceExamples.kr: 방이며 거실이며 집안 전체가 아주 깨끗해요.
sentenceExamples.en: From the room to the living room, the whole house is very clean.
Whether it's math or science, there isn't a subject they're bad at.

sentenceExamples.kr: 옷이며 신발이며 쇼핑을 너무 많이 했어요.
sentenceExamples.en: I did too much shopping, from clothes to shoes.

name: A/V-건 A/V-건 간에
englishMeaning: Whether A or B / Regardless of whether...
briefDescription: Indicates that the result is the same regardless of which option is chosen. Similar to: -든지 (No. 116).
featuredExample: 성공하건 실패하건 간에 최선을 다하는 게 중요해요.
featuredTranslation: Whether you succeed or fail, doing your best is what matters.
longerExplanation: Found in SNU Book 6. This is a highly formal and literary version of the indifference pattern. It is used in debates, news editorials, or formal writing to emphasize that a certain principle or outcome is independent of the listed conditions. '간에' is often added to strengthen the 'regardless' nuance.

sentenceExamples.kr: 비가 오건 눈이 오건 간에 내일 행사는 예정대로 진행됩니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Whether it rains or snows, tomorrow's event will proceed as scheduled.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그가 찬성하건 반대하건 간에 저는 제 결정을 바꾸지 않겠습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Whether he agrees or opposes, I will not change my decision.

sentenceExamples.kr: 음식이 맛있건 맛없건 간에 정성이 들어간 음식은 가치가 있어요.
sentenceExamples.en: Regardless of whether the food is tasty or not, food made with sincerity has value.

name: N을/를 막론하고
englishMeaning: Regardless of N / Irrespective of N
briefDescription: A formal Hanja expression used to show that a fact applies to all members of a category. Similar to: N을/를 불문하고 (No. 320).
featuredExample: 이유 여하를 막론하고 폭력은 정당화될 수 없습니다.
featuredTranslation: Regardless of the reason, violence cannot be justified.
longerExplanation: Found in SNU Book 5. This is a Level 5/6 essential pattern. It uses the Hanja roots 莫 (No) and 論 (Logic/Discussion), literally meaning 'not even needing a discussion.' It is used to generalize a statement across all variables like age, gender, nationality, or rank.

sentenceExamples.kr: 동서고금을 막론하고 효도는 가장 중요한 가치 중 하나입니다.
sentenceExamples.en: Regardless of time or place (East/West, Old/New), filial piety is one of the most important values.

sentenceExamples.kr: 남녀노소를 막론하고 누구나 그 가수의 노래를 좋아해요.
sentenceExamples.en: Irrespective of age or gender, everyone likes that singer's songs.

sentenceExamples.kr: 지위 고하를 막론하고 법은 모든 사람에게 평등하게 적용되어야 한다.
sentenceExamples.en: Regardless of high or low status, the law must be applied equally to all people.

name: N(이)란 N은/는 모두
englishMeaning: Every single N / When it comes to N / All of the N
briefDescription: Used to make a strong, emphatic generalization about every single member of a category.
featuredExample: 맛집이란 맛집은 다 찾아다니는 게 제 취미예요.
featuredTranslation: Seeking out every single famous restaurant there is, is my hobby.
longerExplanation: Found in SNU Book 5. By repeating the noun and using the identifying particle '-(이)란,' the speaker emphasizes the sheer scale or totality of the category. It often carries a nuance of surprise, obsession, or a sense of 'there is nothing left out.'

sentenceExamples.kr: 소문이란 소문은 이미 동네에 다 퍼져서 모르는 사람이 없어요.
sentenceExamples.en: Every single rumor has already spread through the neighborhood, so there is no one who doesn't know.

sentenceExamples.kr: 백화점에 가서 옷이란 옷은 다 입어 본 것 같아요.
sentenceExamples.en: I feel like I tried on every single piece of clothing at the department store.

sentenceExamples.kr: 그는 이번 사건과 관련된 서류란 서류는 모두 검토했습니다.
sentenceExamples.en: He reviewed every single document related to this case.

name: A-(으)ㄴ가?, V-는가?
briefDescription: A formal, written interrogative ending used to ask a question or pose a rhetorical question. Similar to: A/V-(으)ㄴ가/는가 (하다/보다) (No. 296).
featuredTranslation: Is this really true?
longerExplanation: Found in SNU Book 4, pg 72. This is a sentence-final question ending used in writing, news, exams, and rhetorical questions. Attach -(으)ㄴ가? to adjectives (좋은가?, 큰가?), -는가? to verbs and 있다/없다 (가는가?, 있는가?), and -인가? to nouns (학생인가?). It is more literary than -나요? or -습니까?. Do not confuse it with -(으)ㄴ가/는가 하다/보다 (No. 296), which means 'I wonder if / I guess,' or with -(으)ㄴ가/는가 하면 (No. 298), which means 'on the one hand... on the other.'

sentenceExamples.en: Where is he going now?
Is this problem that difficult?
What can we do?
